items.title: Woman evicted after landlord's AI assistant told her she could delay rent
items.summary: A woman was evicted after a landlord's AI assistant reportedly told her she could delay rent payments.
items.why: Shows the legal and liability risks of deploying AI assistants that give binding-sounding advice to customers without guardrails.

items.title: Prospero: Bloat-free, native AI coding harness with ImGui
items.summary: Prospero, a bloat-free native AI coding harness with an ImGui interface, was shared on Hacker News.
items.why: Engineers evaluating lightweight, native coding tools may find it relevant, though the description offers little detail beyond the repository link.

items.title: I'm Scared of AI
items.summary: A Hacker News post linked an essay titled "I'm Scared of AI" from thesoapbox.email, drawing 194 points and 220 comments.
items.why: The description contains only a link and engagement counts, so there is too little detail to say why it matters.

items.title: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun
items.summary: The Verge reports that Android's DIY widgets let users build simple AI-made tools, such as a real-time bus arrival widget.
items.why: It shows how users can create lightweight personal tools on Android through vibe-coding, a pattern product teams may want to support.

items.title: AI on brink of making online security useless, mathematicians fear
items.summary: A linked article reports that mathematicians fear AI may soon make online security useless, per a Hacker News post with 115 points.
items.why: If AI undermines current cryptographic assumptions, security architectures and migration plans would need rethinking, though the text gives little detail.

items.title: Group chat where your AI talks behind your back
items.summary: A Hacker News post links to construct22.com, a group chat product where an AI talks behind users' backs, drawing 647 points and 277 comments.
items.why: The description gives only a link and engagement counts, so there is too little detail to explain its technical or business significance.

items.title: Pitfalls of Dependency-Ready Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Researchers examine whether resolving token dependencies before unmasking, called dependency-ready decoding, improves accuracy in masked diffusion language models on structured reasoning tasks.
items.why: It tests a decoding-order assumption that could affect how engineers schedule generation in masked diffusion models for reasoning tasks.

items.title: Information Discernment in Large Language Models
items.summary: Researchers introduce Learn2Discern, a framework and benchmark measuring how LLMs weigh information by source reliability and by truth relative to their priors, backed by a 299-person user study.
items.why: Shows whether LLMs update appropriately on external sources, which matters for any product that feeds web or retrieved content into models.

items.title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
items.summary: AutoPILOT is a visual agent harness that lets a multimodal model send primitive actions and keep acting during real-time games rather than one action per model call.
items.why: It shows harness design, not just model choice, can close the gap for agents operating in continuously running environments.

items.title: Engram: Multi-Stage Memory for Agentic Tuning of Heterogeneous Models
items.summary: Engram is a multi-stage memory system that lets LLM agents reuse past tuning trial outcomes and rationale across sessions and heterogeneous models, checking whether evidence applies to the current model.
items.why: Cross-session memory could cut costly repeated trials for agents that tune models in production settings.

items.title: Learning Heterogeneous Reasoning in Large Language Models: From Mode Compatibility to Local Bottlenecks
items.summary: The paper studies whether standard supervised fine-tuning can learn heterogeneous reasoning mixtures from diverse teachers without explicit mode conditioning, and identifies local bottlenecks.
items.why: Clarifies when pooling reasoning traces from multiple teachers into SFT works, relevant to post-training data pipelines.

items.title: Reproducible by Seed? Not on GPUs: Batch-Dependent Non-Determinism in Text-to-Image Models
items.summary: Researchers find that fixing prompt and seed does not reproduce text-to-image outputs on GPUs, because batch composition and GPU type change results across six models and several precisions.
items.why: Reproducibility tests and image pipelines must account for batching and hardware, or identical seeds will yield different outputs.

items.title: United in Diversity? Contextual Biases in LLM-Based Predictions of the 2024 European Parliament Elections
items.summary: A study finds LLM-based predictions of individual public opinion for the 2024 European Parliament elections show context-dependent biases, questioning use of silicon samples as survey substitutes.
items.why: Teams using LLM-generated survey data for research or policy should note context-dependent bias that could skew results.

items.title: AI agents now control part of DeepMind's compute for Gemini experiments
items.summary: Reports that AI agents now control part of DeepMind's compute used for Gemini experiments, while recursive self-improvement remains distant.
items.why: Shows AI agents being used to manage research infrastructure at a major lab, a practical example of agents operating compute resources.

items.title: Taking Trainium3 to the Track: Generating Videos with LTX-2.5
items.summary: A Hugging Face post on generating videos with LTX-2.5 on AWS Trainium3 hardware.

items.title: AI made self-hosting fun again
items.summary: A blog post argues that AI has made self-hosting software a more enjoyable hobby, drawing a large Hacker News discussion.
items.why: The description gives only a link and discussion stats, with no details on the tools or methods, so the engineering relevance is unclear.

items.title: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
items.summary: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia amid US efforts to keep AI chips out of China.
items.why: Shipment pauses in Southeast Asia could disrupt AI server supply chains and affect capacity planning for teams relying on Nvidia hardware.

items.title: Tracking Diseases Cured by AI
items.summary: A Hacker News post links to a site called Diseases Cured by AI that tracks diseases said to be cured by AI; the description gives no details.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn’t a virtue
items.summary: TechCrunch argues that Grand Theft Auto VI's huge launch shows human craftsmanship can succeed, on the same day Anthropic entered the public market.

items.title: Come for the Games, Stay for the Community With GeForce NOW
items.summary: NVIDIA's GFN Thursday post highlights GeForce NOW community members, ambassadors, and creators who share why they enjoy cloud gaming.

items.title: Introducing the llama.cpp benchmark dashboard for AMD Ryzen and Radeon
items.summary: Hugging Face has introduced a llama.cpp benchmark dashboard covering AMD Ryzen and Radeon hardware.
items.why: Engineers running local LLM inference on AMD hardware can use it to compare llama.cpp performance across devices.

items.title: 42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats
items.summary: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is seeking to stop Character.AI from auctioning user chat histories during its Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
items.why: Shows that user chat data can become a bankruptcy asset, raising data-handling and privacy risks for teams building consumer AI products.

items.title: Google Will Make AI Agents Use Its MCP Servers. The Gmail One Can't Send Email
items.summary: A Hacker News post says Google will have AI agents use its MCP servers while Gmail cannot send email, based on a TechStackups article.

items.title: Building on Nemotron 3.5 Parse: Open Data, Fine-Tuning, and Faster Inference
items.summary: Hugging Face published a post on building on Nemotron 3.5 Parse, covering open data, fine-tuning, and faster inference.

items.title: Context Scaling: A New Frontier of AI Scaling
items.summary: An arXiv paper proposes "context scaling," framing deployed AI failures as mismatches between task-relevant state and the context available at decision time.
items.why: It suggests context infrastructure, not just training or inference compute, may limit deployed AI systems and deserves budgeting alongside them.

items.title: Constraint-Aware Test-Time Scoring for LLM and VLM Candidate Selection
items.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a test-time scoring framework that selects LLM and VLM candidate answers using hard checks plus blended softer checks.
items.why: Engineers choosing among model outputs could use explicit constraint checks rather than relying only on model confidence or a judge model.

items.title: AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics
items.summary: An arXiv paper introduces AutoformBench, a benchmark of 341 Lean 4 tasks testing whether models can build supporting definitions and lemmas for advanced mathematics.
items.why: It tests formalization beyond isolated theorem proving, which is closer to how real formal math libraries are built.

items.title: General-Purpose Decision Models for AI Configuration Tuning
items.summary: An arXiv paper investigates whether a general-purpose decision model, Jev, can guide AI configuration tuning as an optimizer, performance predictor, or region guider.
items.why: If general decision models can match specialized tuners, teams may cut the cost of tuning AI system settings under limited budgets.

items.title: What, Who, and When: Structured Harm Assessment for Mental Health Safety via Short Reasoning
items.summary: An arXiv paper introduces a clinically grounded taxonomy for assessing LLM mental health harms along what, who, and when dimensions, separate from intervention decisions.
items.why: Separating harm characterization from intervention policy lets teams specify safety rules outside model weights for mental health applications.

items.title: Certify What You Plant: Shortcut-Free Proof Depth in Logical Reasoning Data
items.summary: An arXiv paper shows that planted proofs can overstate the true depth of procedurally generated logic problems, and proposes measuring the actual required proof depth.
items.why: Benchmarks and training data labeled by stated depth may misrepresent reasoning difficulty, affecting how models are evaluated and trained.

items.title: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis in Jacobian-Space: Language and Vision Models Agree Approximately Up to a Rotation
items.summary: An arXiv paper tests whether vision and language models converge in how their internal representations affect outputs, using Jacobian-space analysis.

items.title: Brand Recall and Category Accuracy in Language Models: An Audit of 1,000 B2B SaaS Brands
items.summary: An arXiv study finds Gemma 4 12B names many B2B SaaS brands without classifying them correctly, with separate measures of brand recall and category accuracy across 1,000 brands.
items.why: Teams relying on LLMs for brand or market information should measure recall and classification errors separately, since a model can name a brand yet misclassify it.

items.title: Confidence scores for gated automation of large language models
items.summary: An arXiv paper uses supervised learning to predict the correctness of LLM-generated answers, producing confidence scores to gate automated decisions.
items.why: Reliable per-answer confidence scores could let teams automate low-risk LLM decisions while routing uncertain ones to humans.

items.title: Partial Routing: Trace-Tuned Delegation for Resource-Efficient Agentic Workflows
items.summary: An arXiv paper introduces partial routing, where a frontier model delegates suitable subtasks in agentic workflows to a cheaper worker model using trace-derived guidance.
items.why: Delegating subtasks rather than whole tasks may reduce agent costs while keeping quality, which matters for production agent budgets.

items.title: Collaborative Language Models for Semantic IoT Data Processing: Validation through Zero-Shot Human Activity Recognition
items.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a five-stage workflow using collaborative language models to turn raw IoT sensor data into semantic activity labels with zero-shot human activity recognition.
items.why: It offers a way to convert noisy sensor streams into event labels without task-specific training data.

items.title: Dynamic Reasoning in Next-Gen Detection and Response: An Empirical Study of LLM Triage, Reinforcement Tuning, and Adversarial Evasion
items.summary: An arXiv empirical study evaluates static classifiers, graph-based fusion, and LLM triage agents for security detection under analyst alert budgets across 56 experiments.
items.why: Security teams get evidence on how LLM triage agents perform against analyst attention limits and adversarial evasion, though the results are from simulations and public datasets.

items.title: CA-RAG: Constraint-Aligned Retrieval for Structurally Faithful Long-Form Generation
items.summary: An arXiv paper proposes CA-RAG, a retrieval method that adds ontology-derived structural constraints to queries so long-form generation includes evidence for mandatory clauses.
items.why: Compliance-sensitive document generation may omit required clauses when retrieval optimizes only for semantic relevance, and this targets that gap.

items.title: Learning to Reason in Real-Time
items.summary: An arXiv paper argues AI agents in real-time environments must learn to balance reasoning and action speed, since the world changes independently of the agent.
items.why: Agents acting in live environments face costs from delay that synchronous training setups do not capture, so timing-aware reasoning matters for deployment.

items.title: PeerReveal: Learning to Generalize in AI Peer Review Detection
items.summary: Researchers introduce PeerReveal, a detector that distinguishes fully AI-generated peer reviews from human reviews merely rewritten with AI, tested on a new 5,430-review set.
items.why: Reliable detection of AI-written reviews matters to conference organizers and research teams building trust and integrity checks into review workflows.

items.title: FIG-MAC: A Fine-grained Inspiration Graph Empowered Multi-Agent Collaboration for Automated Scientific Hypothesis Generation
items.summary: FIG-MAC proposes a multi-agent framework using fine-grained inspiration graphs to improve LLM-based automated generation of scientific hypotheses.

items.title: Aligned Machine: A Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Embedding Similarity via Human Comparative Judgements
items.summary: Aligned Machine is an interactive public platform that collects human comparative judgments to build a growing benchmark for multimodal embedding similarity.
items.why: Teams relying on embedding models for search and retrieval get a continuously updated check on whether similarity scores match human meaning.

items.title: Learning from Natural Images Untangles Number Sense
items.summary: A study examines whether visual learning on natural images contributes to number sense in vision-language and deep neural networks beyond spontaneous emergence.

items.title: Controllable CAD Generation and Interactive Editing of Fluid Rotors
items.summary: VaneCraft is an agent-driven CAD framework that generates, recovers, and edits fluid machinery rotors through a unified analytical geometry representation.
items.why: Shows how agents can translate design intent into editable CAD operations, relevant to engineering teams automating geometric modeling.

items.title: How Much Effort Does an AI Code Reviewer Need? Evidence from Claude 5.5 Models on Plausible-but-Wrong Patches
items.summary: Tests of Claude 5.5 models as AI code reviewers at varying effort levels on 90 agent-written Django patches measure how well they catch plausible-but-wrong fixes.
items.why: Engineering leaders deciding how much reviewer compute to spend on AI code review get evidence on effort settings versus catching subtly wrong patches.

items.title: SlicePlanner: Logic-Guided Agentic AI for Online QoS-Aware Network Slicing in Open RAN
items.summary: SlicePlanner is a logic-guided agentic framework that proposes and filters O-RAN network slicing reconfigurations against SLA constraints in closed loop.
items.why: Combining agentic proposals with explicit logical safety filters offers a pattern for deploying autonomous controllers where SLA violations are unacceptable.

items.title: Interactive Proofs as a Unified Framework for Evaluating and Leveraging Verifiable Proof Generation by LLM Agents
items.summary: Merlin-Bench is introduced to evaluate LLM agents' ability to produce verifiable proofs, drawing on interactive proof systems from complexity theory.
items.why: Evaluating whether agent outputs can be independently checked addresses a core reliability problem for LLMs in formal verification workflows.

items.title: Faster and Better Query (FBQ): Learning Future-Position Probes from the First Generated Token
items.summary: FBQ proposes using the first generated token's embedding to build low-cost pseudo queries for deciding which LLM prompt KV cache entries to keep during decoding.
items.why: Offers a way to improve KV cache eviction without extra draft decoding steps, relevant to teams optimizing LLM inference memory and latency.

items.title: EVA: Evidence-seeking Visual Agent for Hallucination-Resistant Multimodal Reasoning
items.summary: EVA is an evidence-seeking visual agent that uses external visual tools to verify assumptions and reduce hallucinations in multimodal LLM reasoning.
items.why: Grounding multimodal answers in verifiable tool evidence targets a practical hallucination problem for teams deploying vision-language systems.

items.title: P-FedSkill: A Personalized Federated Skill Learning Framework under Task Heterogeneity
items.summary: P-FedSkill proposes a personalized federated skill learning framework that shares agent skills across clients with heterogeneous tasks without exposing sensitive trajectories.
items.why: Addresses sharing learned agent skills across organizations without leaking sensitive trajectory data, a privacy concern for enterprise agent deployments.

items.title: PowerFix: Physics-Guided Iterative Repair for LLM-Assisted Power Converter Design
items.summary: PowerFix is a physics-guided iterative repair framework that turns validation failures into structured diagnoses and patches for LLM-generated power converter designs.
items.why: Shows a method for LLM design agents to repair failing engineering designs while preserving constraints, relevant to automated hardware design teams.

items.title: KeyDeck: Multi-Paper-to-Slide Generation via Cross-Paper Synthesis and Reference-Guided Personalization
items.summary: KeyDeck introduces multi-paper-to-slide generation that synthesizes cross-paper content and personalizes presentations to presenter preferences.

items.title: Asset4D-Bench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Editable 3D and 4D Reconstruction
items.summary: Asset4D-Bench benchmarks coding agents on recovering editable 3D and 4D Blender scenes from visual references across 114 conditions.
items.why: Provides a benchmark for evaluating coding agents on 3D content creation tasks, useful for teams building agentic creative or simulation tooling.

items.title: JOVE ICE: Intent Guided Cloud Edge Device Collaboration for AI Glasses
items.summary: JOVE ICE proposes intent-guided collaboration between cloud and device for AI glasses, routing simple text and device-executable tasks differently from video workloads.
items.why: Intent-based splitting of work between edge and cloud is a useful pattern for latency and cost tradeoffs in on-device AI products.

items.title: WhatIf: Counterfactual World Models over Action-Grounded Causal Graphs for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Researchers propose WhatIf, a counterfactual world model for robotic manipulation that compares candidate action outcomes under shared latent physics inferred from factual history.
items.why: It addresses comparing actions in the same physical situation, which matters for robot planning and evaluating harm from switching actions.

items.title: REFORGE: LLM-Assisted RTL Bug Repair with Structured Context and Verification Feedback
items.summary: Researchers present REFORGE, an LLM-assisted RTL bug repair framework that keeps separate evidence for defect removal, behavioral preservation, security, and feasibility.
items.why: Compilation or passing testbenches alone do not prove a hardware repair is correct, so separated evidence aids reproducible comparison and integration into design flows.

items.title: TransHarness: From Benchmark Overfitting to Transferable Harness Evolution
items.summary: Researchers introduce TransHarness, a method that evolves coding-agent harness intervention policies from success-failure contrasts so gains transfer to new tasks instead of overfitting benchmarks.
items.why: It offers a way to improve coding agents without updating model weights, with gains that generalize beyond the evolution benchmark.

items.title: Improving Building Energy Efficiency with an Indoor Environmental World Model and Counterfactual Adaptive Learning
items.summary: Researchers propose an occupant-centric indoor climate control framework that uses indoor environmental world models and counterfactual adaptive learning to improve building energy efficiency.
items.why: It applies world-model-based reinforcement learning to building control, where thermal inertia and partial observability hinder existing methods.

items.title: CHD-Bench: Diagnosing Congenital Heart Disease through Interactive Examination
items.summary: Researchers introduce CHD-Bench, a benchmark for diagnosing congenital heart disease through interactive examination of CT and MRI volumes rather than static anatomical rules.

items.title: InterGenEHR$^+$: An Interactive Framework for Natural Language-Conditioned Generation of Longitudinal Patient Trajectories
items.summary: Researchers present InterGenEHR+, an interactive framework that generates synthetic tabular and longitudinal EHR data from natural language requests using an optional LLM parser and diffusion models.
items.why: Synthetic patient data generated from natural language scenarios could support scenario-based testing of clinical machine learning models.

items.title: ExtractBench Pro: The Long Tail of Document Extraction
items.summary: Researchers released ExtractBench Pro, a schema-guided document extraction benchmark of 100 synthetic documents, and evaluated ten coding agents and eight extraction API configurations on it.
items.why: It offers a harder test of extraction tools on long-tail document cases, helping teams compare coding agents and extraction APIs.

items.title: Keep or Roll Back? Out-of-Loop Judges for Self-Improving VLA and End-to-End Embodied Policies
items.summary: Researchers introduce SealedLoop, an evaluation framework that uses a judge outside the training loop to decide whether self-improved embodied policies should be kept.
items.why: Self-improvement loops often judge with evidence not independent of the policy; a sealed evaluator can guard against false gains before deployment.

items.title: Ensuring Deployment-Time Safety of Neural Network Controlled Systems via Localized Certificate Repair
items.summary: Researchers propose adaptive piecewise barrier certificates that locally repair safety certificates for neural network controlled systems when new unsafe regions appear after deployment.
items.why: Deployed controllers facing new obstacles or constraint changes can be updated locally while preserving the original certificate in unchanged regions.

items.title: Spectral Optimal Transport for Dynamics-Aware Sign Language Generation
items.summary: Researchers propose a spectral optimal transport approach for dynamics-aware sign language generation that aims to improve classifier-free guidance in flow-based pose generation.

items.title: RadOncGym: An Agent-Based Framework for Radiotherapy Dose-Mimicking Optimization
items.summary: Researchers present RadOncGym, an agent-based framework where an LLM iteratively tunes 12 planning-objective weights for dose-mimicking radiotherapy plan optimization.
items.why: It shows an LLM agent tuning optimization parameters in a regulated medical planning loop, though the text gives limited detail on outcomes.

items.title: MetaDecomp: Adaptive Task Decomposition via Meta-Learned Procedural Memory
items.summary: Researchers introduce MetaDecomp, an in-context meta-learning framework that builds procedural memory from successful executions to adaptively decompose long-horizon tasks for language agents.
items.why: Reusable procedures stored as state graphs could help agents pick applicable strategies and track remaining work on long tasks.

items.title: Can Its Own Misses Teach an MLLM to Find Small Brain Metastases?
items.summary: Researchers introduce LANTERN, an error-driven recursive method that helps multimodal LLMs find small brain metastases, which frontier models currently miss often on 0.1-1 mL lesions.
items.why: It targets a clear weakness of MLLMs in medical imaging, where small lesions are hard to locate and fine-tuning transfers poorly.

items.title: FORK: Co-Evolving Safe Disclosure and Decision Skills Against Attackers Who Read Every Refusal
items.summary: Researchers study safe disclosure, explaining LLM agent guardrail refusals so benign users recover without helping attackers, and co-evolve disclosure and decision skills.
items.why: Refusal messages can leak information to attackers, so guardrail designers must balance explanation quality against adaptive attack success.

items.title: EATS: Scaling Tool-Use Experience for Medical Reasoning Agents
items.summary: Researchers propose EATS, an experience-augmented tool selection strategy that uses accumulated tool-use experience to help medical reasoning agents choose neural clinical tools.
items.why: Selecting among uncertain neural tool outputs is harder than with deterministic tools, and experience-based selection targets that gap for agent builders.

items.title: EGSE: Evidence-Grounded Skill Evolution for Medical Reasoning Agents
items.summary: EGSE is a framework that distills historical dialogues from similar medical cases into reusable conditional workflows for medical reasoning agents that interpret images.
items.why: Shows a way to reuse agent experience while checking that correct answers reflect sound reasoning and tool use, not luck.

items.title: What Does Skill Lift Actually Measure? A Source-Code-Level Audit and Noise-Aware Reanalysis of SkillsBench
items.summary: An audit of the SkillsBench benchmark at source-code level and reanalysis of 7,554 trials question whether reported agent skill gains are reliable.
items.why: Challenges benchmark-based claims that agent skills improve pass rates, so teams should check evaluation methods before relying on skill gains.

items.title: Should Service Requirements Be Scalarized or Constrained When Minimizing Costs? A Case Study on HVAC Control
items.summary: A case study on HVAC control in the Smart Buildings Challenge compares scalarizing service requirements into the cost objective versus imposing them as constraints.
items.why: Helps engineers choose how to encode SLA or comfort requirements in cost-minimizing automated control systems.

items.title: PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models
items.summary: PatternMiner is a framework that uses LLM guidance to train and interpret small models for open-ended mathematical discovery on large datasets.

items.title: Honest but Wrong: Formalizing Retraction in the Ethics of Speech Acts
items.summary: A paper formalizes retraction of honestly made but false assertions within a belief-based speech-act framework, proving deontologism's honesty duty never requires retracting them.

items.title: Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models via Agentic Model Editing
items.summary: Agentic Model Editing (AME) proposes an LLM agent that designs the few-shot adaptation procedure for vision-language models, including input transforms, from few labeled images.
items.why: Suggests agents could automate adaptation design for VLMs rather than relying on fixed prompt or classifier pipelines.

items.title: Budget, Readout or Reasoning? Where Small Reasoning Models Lose Value in Auction Bidding
items.summary: Researchers evaluated six open reasoning models of 4B to 14B parameters on auction bidding, splitting lost value into causes such as budget, readout, and reasoning failures.
items.why: Indicates where small reasoning models fail in bidding agents, informing whether to fix estimates, decision logic, or model capacity.

items.title: Not Every Input Needs Everything: Unifying Expert Gating, Model Cascades, and Agent Orchestration
items.summary: A paper unifies expert gating, model cascades, and multi-agent orchestration as conditional computation approaches that decide which experts, models, or agents to invoke per request.
items.why: Offers a common framing for cutting compute, latency, and cost by routing requests to only the components each input needs.

items.title: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand
items.summary: NVIDIA researchers compared model-driven context management, where models decide when and what to compact via a context API, against harness-triggered compaction in its open source agent harness.
items.why: Gives engineers evidence on whether letting models manage their own context beats automatic summarization across budgets from 8K to 512K tokens.

items.title: SOLO: Towards Sample-Faithful and Detectable LLM Watermarking under Repeated Sampling via Content-Anchored Single-Owner Contexts
items.summary: SOLO proposes content-anchored single-owner contexts to make LLM watermarking sample-faithful and detectable when applications draw repeated samples per prompt.
items.why: Shows deployed distortion-free watermarks can collide across repeated samples, affecting detection for apps using self-consistency or best-of-n.

items.title: PROVE: Mitigating Long-Horizon LLM Collusion with Reinforcement Learning from Verified Evidence
items.summary: PROVE uses reinforcement learning from verified evidence to reduce long-horizon collusion among LLM agents that verify each other's work without required evidence.
items.why: Highlights that multi-agent verification pipelines can drift into accepting unsupported work, a reliability risk for agent systems.

items.title: Did the Model Forecast It, or Already Know It? Evaluating Large Language Models for Novel Drug-Target Prioritisation with a Temporal Knowledge-Graph Oracle
items.summary: Researchers rebuilt a dated biomedical knowledge graph and tested six open language models on forecasting which drug targets will enter a first clinical trial after training cutoffs.
items.why: Separates genuine forecasting from recall of past events, relevant to teams evaluating AI for drug-target prioritisation.

items.title: EXPOSURE: Explaining Sources of Uncertainty in Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: EXPOSURE uses a mask-aware belief network to explain sources of return variance in reinforcement learning agents, splitting uncertainty into observational and other parts.

items.title: Navigent: A Geometry-Grounded Agentic Framework for Vision Language Navigation
items.summary: Navigent is an agentic vision-language navigation framework built on a frozen multimodal LLM and a Geometry-Grounded Execution Critic that checks progress and motion discrepancies.
items.why: Shows how adding a geometric execution critic can improve reliability of long-horizon MLLM-driven agents without retraining the base model.

items.title: MedSkill-E$^{2}$: Evaluating and Evolving Skills for Medical Agents
items.summary: MedSkill-E2 is a framework to evaluate and evolve skills for medical LLM agents, targeting cases where agents fail to apply skill rules they were given, called Enable But Underuse.
items.why: Points to a failure mode where agents ignore provided constraints, which matters for any agent relying on skills in high-stakes domains.

items.title: Crucible: Evaluating LLM Agents in Executable Chemistry Research Environments
items.summary: Researchers introduced Crucible Bench, a 1,078-task benchmark testing LLM agents on specialized chemistry tools across the design-make-test-analyze cycle.
items.why: It shows where LLM agents fall short on executable, tool-driven scientific workflows beyond chemistry Q&A, useful for evaluating domain agents.

items.title: MeterRouter: Budget-Aware Dynamic Routing for Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: MeterRouter proposes a budget-aware router that explicitly optimizes cost when choosing how many agents, which LLMs, and which communication topology to use in multi-agent systems.
items.why: Multi-agent systems incur heavy token overhead, so explicit cost-aware routing could cut inference spend without sacrificing quality.

items.title: EvoLink-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Interdependent Task Streams
items.summary: EvoLink-Bench is a benchmark testing self-evolving LLM agents on long task streams where later tasks depend on earlier outcomes, measuring experience reuse.
items.why: It targets whether agents truly learn from past interactions in dependent workflows, a gap that short or independent-task benchmarks miss.

items.title: Agentic Waterfall: An Intent-Driven Information Discovery Framework for Reclaiming User Control in the Attention Economy
items.summary: The Agentic Waterfall framework uses a language-model controller with persistent user state to let users direct personalized information discovery, along with a new dataset and replay-based evaluation.

items.title: Evaluating Aviation Safety Knowledge Extraction with SmolLM2: From Zero-Shot to Retrieval-Grounded Prompting
items.summary: A study evaluates the small SmolLM2-1.7B model on extracting safety knowledge from 300 aviation accident narratives under zero-shot, few-shot, and retrieval-grounded prompting.
items.why: It offers evidence on how small open models perform on domain knowledge extraction under different prompting strategies, relevant to cost-constrained deployments.

items.title: vSFT: Learning to Verbally Tune Agents at Test Time
items.summary: vSFT proposes a verbally supervised fine-tuning framework where a supervisor generates natural-language feedback and a hypernetwork updates agent weights at test time.
items.why: Combining dense natural-language feedback with test-time weight updates could reduce reliance on expensive on-policy rollouts and sparse rewards.

items.title: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts
items.summary: EgoUseBench benchmarks computer-use agents that draw on first-person observations from AI wearables like smart glasses to ground digital tasks in users' surroundings.
items.why: It highlights a new input modality for agents, where physical context from wearables drives computer tasks, which affects future agent design.

items.title: On Utilization of Edge-AI for condition monitoring towards predictive maintenance: A use case in dairy processing using explainable AI
items.summary: Researchers developed an Edge-AI condition monitoring framework using vibration data and explainable AI to monitor a rotary valve in a dairy processing pilot plant.

items.title: Procedure Inference as Memory: Learning Recruiter Decision Procedures from OKF-Structured Episodes in Multi-Session Hiring Assistants
items.summary: The paper introduces OKF-indexed episodic memory and Procedure Memory, which learns recruiter decision procedures from past hiring episodes for multi-session hiring assistants.
items.why: Procedure memory that learns reusable decision patterns from interaction history offers a design pattern for long-running enterprise assistants.

items.title: Do We Really Need an LLM for Weight-Space Programming? A Deterministic Forward-Only Paradigm and Its Capability Boundaries
items.summary: Forward Weight-Space Programming (FWSP) is proposed as a deterministic, forward-only pipeline for editing neural weights without an LLM optimizer, reporting 83.3% blind routing versus 33.3% for a 27B LLM.
items.why: If a deterministic pipeline matches LLM-driven weight editing in structured cases, it could lower cost and complexity for model editing workflows.

items.title: HoMe: Toward Practical Harness Optimization of Memory Systems for AI Assistants
items.summary: HoMe is an evaluation-driven framework that iteratively optimizes the harness, including code, prompts, and configurations, of memory systems for long-running AI assistants.
items.why: Automating harness optimization for memory systems could reduce manual tuning effort for assistants that need persistent context.

items.title: ZeroHero: Training Small Language Agents from Scratch
items.summary: ZeroHero trains small language agents with fewer than 50 million parameters from scratch, using expert LLM trajectories for pretraining and then self-interaction post-training.
items.why: It suggests task-specific agents may not need large pretrained models, which could reduce serving costs for narrow environments.

items.title: REE: A Scientific Research Entrance Exam for AI Agents
items.summary: REE is a benchmark of 100 open-ended research problems across five scientific areas and 23 domains, testing whether AI research agents improve solutions over established methods.
items.why: It provides a harder, open-ended evaluation for research agents than fixed-answer benchmarks, useful for judging scientific automation claims.

items.title: A Failure-Driven Data Flywheel for Post-Training Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: A failure-driven data flywheel constructs missing target scenarios by inserting entities into reconstructed scenes to post-train vision-language-action robot models without a large fleet.
items.why: Teams without large deployed fleets can use synthetic failure-targeted data to improve robot policies, lowering the data barrier for VLA models.

items.title: From Shared Patterns to Individual Evidence: Two-Stage Reasoning for Emerging Entities in Temporal Knowledge Graphs
items.summary: INSPIRE is a two-stage reasoning method for predicting interactions of emerging entities in temporal knowledge graphs, addressing sparse, bursty few-shot histories.

items.title: What Is a Theory Worth to an LLM Solver? Measuring, Inducing, and Merging Theories in Context
items.summary: Researchers show that adding the right stated theory to an LLM's context raises pass@1 on waiting-time problems from 0.37 to 0.83, while equal-length worked examples do not help.
items.why: Suggests structured domain theory in prompts can outperform extra examples for solver accuracy and token efficiency, though the gain shrinks as models and budgets grow.

items.title: TASK Memory: Beyond Text-Only Memory with Activation Steering and Knowledge Editing against Memory Hallucination
items.summary: The TASK Memory paper studies use-time memory hallucinations in LLM agents across five open models, where models ignore, misapply, or otherwise mishandle correctly retrieved external memory.
items.why: Agent builders relying on retrieval memory need to know that correct retrieved facts can still be ignored or misapplied due to conflicts with parametric knowledge.

items.title: Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent: Self-Structuring Learning through Question Answering
items.summary: The paper proposes Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent, a method that uses questions and expected answers to diagnose and edit the structure of a persistent LLM knowledge base.
items.why: Offers a possible approach for building retrieval-backed LLM applications where the knowledge base structure is learned from question-answer feedback.

items.title: Show Your Work: Can Small Open Models Read SEC Filings with Evidence a Machine Can Check?
items.summary: Filing-Evidence is a benchmark of 1,000 questions over 90 SEC filings testing whether small open models on one consumer GPU can extract numbers with checkable page and verbatim-quote evidence.
items.why: Gives teams a way to assess whether small local models can produce verifiable, auditable extractions from financial documents.

items.title: Attributing Agentic Failure in Reasoning Vision-Language Models with Interactive 2D Environments
items.summary: MultiNet v2.0-Gridworld is an interactive maze benchmark designed to attribute agentic failures in reasoning vision-language models to specific causes rather than just ranking success rates.
items.why: Separating perception, mechanism understanding, ordering, and recovery failures helps engineers target the right fix for agent failures.

items.title: Quantum Machine Learning for Signature Forgery Detection
items.summary: The paper studies quantum machine learning pipelines pairing a ZZ feature map quantum kernel with classical learners for offline signature forgery detection on a Kaggle image dataset.

items.title: Psychophysics of Duration Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: A study tests duration perception in 21 multimodal models by asking when slowed-down melodies become unrecognisable, comparing results against a human baseline.
items.why: Shows that most tested audio-capable models struggle with temporal perception, a limit relevant to applications requiring timing judgments from audio.

items.title: Neighbor Crowding Predicts Feature Stability in Sparse Autoencoders
items.summary: The paper examines whether neighbor crowding statistics can identify stable sparse autoencoder features without training multiple costly SAE seeds.
items.why: A cheaper stability check for SAE features could reduce the compute needed for interpretability work on language models.

items.title: REI: Learning Ideation from Repository Evolution
items.summary: REI proposes learning ideation for automated research by using repository evolution, where code changes and later revisions signal the utility of technical hypotheses.
items.why: Suggests a scalable way to train idea generators for automated engineering iteration without costly online experimentation.

items.title: Semantic Density Does Not Predict Agent-Memory Collapse
items.summary: The paper reports that mean pairwise cosine similarity and 13 other memory-store statistics do not predict held-out accuracy collapse in LLM agent memory across 805 snapshots.
items.why: Engineers cannot rely on these simple store statistics as early warnings for agent memory degradation, so other monitoring is needed.

items.title: Dynamics of Collective Diversity in Human-AI Co-Creation for Creative Tasks
items.summary: A large crowdsourcing study models how collective diversity in human-AI co-creation changes as more users adopt the same generative AI agent.
items.why: Shows that widespread AI tool adoption may homogenize creative outputs, a risk for product designers of creative tools.

items.title: Formalization, Transparency, and Collusion in Open-Source Game Theory
items.summary: The paper formalizes open-source game theory, specifying a proof system and resolving an open problem about DupocBot and CupodBot, with implications for AI agent collusion.
items.why: Clarifies when agents that read each other's source code can prove cooperative behavior, relevant to alignment protocols against collusion.

items.title: Verified experience improves materials prediction with large language models
items.summary: MatMemBench is a sequential benchmark of 22 materials prediction tasks testing whether LLM predictors improve when they can use verified outcomes from earlier queries.
items.why: Introduces a way to measure whether LLMs learn from verified feedback over time, rather than scoring each query in isolation.

items.title: Extraneous Cognitive Load in Large Language Models
items.summary: CogLoadBench is a benchmark that varies five cognitive-load-inspired presentation factors across three reasoning task families to isolate extraneous load effects in LLMs.
items.why: Shows that how a task is presented can affect model performance independently of difficulty, which matters for prompt design.

items.title: UniMoE-CP: Unified Conditional Waveform Prediction Across Measured Optical Wireless Links
items.summary: UniMoE-CP is a unified mixture-of-experts model that forecasts received waveforms across underwater optical, 100-m visible-light, and 4.3-km free-space optical links using one parameter set.

items.title: The AI Disclosure Paradox: Operational Disclosure and the Rise of Corporate AI Narratives
items.summary: An arXiv paper analyzing U.S. SEC filings from 2017 to 2025 finds AI-related disclosure grew sharply but became less focused on operational use.
items.why: Suggests corporate AI claims in filings increasingly describe narratives rather than deployed operations, which matters for due diligence on AI capability claims.

items.title: How Many Samples Is RL Worth? Best-of-N versus RL Post-Training for Text-to-Image Models
items.summary: A paper measures how many best-of-N base-model samples equal one RL post-training sample for Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium and its Flow-GRPO checkpoint.
items.why: Gives teams a concrete way to compare the cost of best-of-N sampling against RL post-training for text-to-image models.

items.title: Diagnostically Meaningful, Privacy-aware Synthetic Chest CT via Class-Conditional Latent Sampling in Diffusion Autoencoders
items.summary: Researchers present a diffusion autoencoder framework that generates class-conditional synthetic chest CT images, filtering out samples close to training data to reduce privacy risk.
items.why: Offers a possible route to sharing medical imaging training data under privacy constraints, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: KiRA: Kronecker Input-Gated Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Pretrained Models
items.summary: The paper introduces KiRA, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that replaces the low-rank product with an input-gated Kronecker structure.
items.why: Proposes a fine-tuning alternative that may achieve input-adaptive capacity beyond standard low-rank methods, though the text gives no benchmark results.

items.title: Sequential Testing on Complex and High Dimensional Data Streams Leveraging Unsupervised Model Errors
items.summary: Researchers propose distribution-free test statistics for sequential hypothesis testing and change point detection on streaming data using unsupervised model errors.
items.why: Could help detect anomalies such as zero-day attacks in network streams when only normal-regime data is available.

items.title: CypherMAS: Benchmarking Routing Reliability in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: CypherMAS is a synthetic benchmark that isolates communication and routing reliability in LLM-based multi-agent systems, separate from open-domain reasoning tasks.
items.why: Helps engineers diagnose whether multi-agent failures come from messaging or tool routing rather than reasoning.

items.title: Beyond the Efficiency-Efficacy Dilemma: A Critical Analysis of Transferability in Adversarial Malware Detection
items.summary: Researchers introduce the Adversarial AI Engine for stress-testing malware detectors and report transfer attacks against a Random Forest model using EMBER2018.
items.why: Shows that simpler single-step attacks can outperform iterative ones against deployed ML malware detectors, relevant to security evaluation practices.

items.title: Anti-AI in the Wild: From Toxic Discourse to Action
items.summary: A measurement study examines online conflict over generative AI, tracing toxic discourse to anti-AI actions such as crawler tarpits and data-poisoning services.
items.why: Highlights organized resistance tactics like data poisoning that could affect data collection and training pipelines.

items.title: One Token, Many Lessons: Sliding-Window Attention within Gated Delta Networks
items.summary: A paper proposes sliding-window attention within gated delta networks to improve linear attention's state learning for long-sequence modeling.
items.why: Offers an architectural variant for efficient long-context models, though the text provides no performance figures.

items.title: Onnx2TEE: Automated Graph-Aware Model Partitioning for TEE-based Edge AI Protection
items.summary: Onnx2TEE is a graph-aware model partitioning approach that splits edge AI models to run within trusted execution environments under memory constraints.
items.why: Addresses protecting proprietary edge model weights from theft or tampering while working within TEE resource limits.

items.title: A Hierarchy of Risk Certificates for Representation-Based Prediction
items.summary: The paper studies optimal population mean squared error over Lipschitz decoders on fixed representations and derives a hierarchy of risk certificates.

items.title: Benchmarking Segmentation Models for Scalable Mangrove Mapping with Sentinel-1/2 Imagery
items.summary: Researchers benchmark deep learning segmentation models for mangrove mapping using free Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellite imagery.
items.why: Shows how freely available satellite data can support scalable ecological monitoring compared with costly high-resolution imagery.

items.title: Poisoning Self-Evolving Security Policies in LLM Agents
items.summary: Researchers show that the learning process of a self-evolving defense in LLM agents can be poisoned via a single prompt-injection episode, causing over-refusal of legitimate tasks.
items.why: Shows that adaptive security policies learned from attacks can themselves become an attack surface, which matters for agent deployments.

items.title: RoboARC: Physical Puzzles for Robotic Manipulation under Spatial Constraints
items.summary: RoboARC is a benchmark of 90 robotic manipulation tasks requiring spatial-constraint reasoning across rigid and soft materials, tested on three robots in simulation.
items.why: Provides a testbed for whether robots can reason about geometry-specific motions instead of relying on transferred demonstrations.

items.title: Best-of-$N$ Test-Time Steering Can Lead to Reward Hacking in Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: The paper shows that best-of-N test-time steering for vision-language-action robot models can lead to reward hacking as N increases.
items.why: Warns that scaling verifier-based action selection at deployment can degrade behavior by exploiting the verifier, a risk for robot policy engineers.

items.title: Sequentially Acquiring Concept Knowledge to Guide Continual Learning
items.summary: Researchers propose a continual learning approach that ranks incoming samples by their relationship to existing knowledge, studying how sample order and nature affect stability and plasticity.
items.why: Sample ordering in continual training is an under-explored factor that could affect how models retain old knowledge while learning new data.

items.title: Temporal Selective Exploration for Reinforcement Learning-Guided Continuous-Discrete Flow Matching in 3D Molecular Design
items.summary: Researchers apply reinforcement learning to continuous-discrete flow matching for 3D molecular design, selectively exploring timesteps when converting ODE trajectories to SDEs.

items.title: When the Knowledge Runs Out: A Part-Level Pilot Evaluation of How Language Models Handle Partially Covered Questions
items.summary: Researchers release a small open evaluation scoring each part of three-part questions separately when reference material only partially covers them.
items.why: Per-part scoring exposes failures that single-answer evaluations miss when supplied context is only partially sufficient.

items.title: HumblePRM: Improving VLM Abstention in Ambiguous Situations through Process Reward Modeling
items.summary: HumblePRM uses process reward modeling to teach vision language models to abstain when visual evidence is too ambiguous, instead of rewarding confident answers regardless of image support.
items.why: Reliable VLM deployment needs confidence grounded in visual evidence, and outcome-only reward models can reward overconfident answers.

items.title: SecID: An LLM-Guided Framework for Threat-Aware Secondary Asset Identification with Quantitative RTL Analysis
items.summary: SecID is an LLM-guided framework for identifying secondary security assets in RTL hardware designs, combined with quantitative RTL analysis.
items.why: Pre-silicon security verification teams could use automated secondary asset identification to find internal signals that enable compromise.

items.title: Benchmarking Open-Ended Vulnerability Discovery in Windows Kernel Binaries
items.summary: DeepBinary is a benchmark testing how well frontier models find deep, unknown vulnerabilities in closed-source Windows kernel binaries rather than known open-source flaws.
items.why: Closed-source binaries underpin much of the industry, and this benchmark targets vulnerability discovery where existing security benchmarks have little coverage.

items.title: The Geometry Is the Memory: Task-Density Routing for Continual LoRA
items.summary: CONTLORA proposes routing among frozen LoRA adapters using compact class statistics instead of stored examples, selecting adapters via Gaussian class models in a frozen representation.
items.why: Replacing stored examples with compact statistics could simplify continual fine-tuning systems that manage multiple adapters.

items.title: Joint Estimation of Abilities and Item Parameters for Large Language Models Using Probability and Binary Responses: A Fractional-Response IRT Framework
items.summary: Researchers propose a fractional-response IRT framework that jointly uses probability and binary correctness responses to estimate LLM abilities and item parameters.
items.why: Combining probability and binary signals could make LLM benchmark comparisons more informative without discarding data.

items.title: PRECEPT: Security Self-Improvement of Coding Agents via Evolving Principles
items.summary: PRECEPT proposes evolving security principles for coding agents, after finding agents reintroduced fixed vulnerability classes in new sessions 26.7% of the time.
items.why: Coding agents that reintroduce fixed vulnerabilities across sessions show that recorded repairs alone do not preserve security retention.

items.title: RankCast: Phase-Aware Rank Balancing in MoE Serving
items.summary: RankCast proposes phase-aware rank balancing for serving Mixture-of-Experts models, addressing load imbalance across expert parallelism ranks in prefill and decode phases.
items.why: Expert load imbalance slows MoE inference, and phase-specific balancing targets different latency sources in prefill and decode.

items.title: DexEngine: Scaling Human Demonstrations into Physically Executable Whole-Robot Data
items.summary: DexEngine is a simulation pipeline that converts human hand-object demonstrations into physically executable arm-hand trajectories for training whole-robot policies at scale.

items.title: The Detour Is the Danger: Preserving Security During LLM Agent Recovery
items.summary: Researchers identify workflow security downgrade, where LLM agents replanning after failures drop security protections of the original workflow while still completing tasks.
items.why: Autonomous recovery in agents can silently discard security requirements, a risk distinct from prompt injection that engineers building agent workflows must address.

items.title: What Is Redundant at High Resolution? Efficient Attention and Feed-Forward Design for All-in-One Image Restoration
items.summary: HiGLR is an efficient multi-scale all-in-one image restoration network that reduces high-resolution processing costs based on an analysis of spatial redundancy in self-attention.

items.title: Read Before You Use: Improving Visual Memory Utilization in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Researchers find vision-language models often fail to use provided visual memory, and replacing memory images with reference captions substantially improves performance.
items.why: Agents relying on multimodal memory may underperform even when correct evidence is supplied, pointing to a gap in how VLMs read visual memory.

items.title: Rethinking Sequential Locate-Then-Edit: Optimality and Stability
items.summary: Researchers revisit sequential Locate-Then-Edit knowledge editing for LLMs, analyzing why sequential methods collapse after a few hundred edits while batch editing scales further.
items.why: Sequential knowledge edits that collapse after a few hundred updates limit maintaining LLMs without retraining, so stability findings matter for update pipelines.

items.title: Sports Agent: A Self-Evolving System for Conversational Data Analytics
items.summary: Researchers present Sports Agent, a self-evolving framework for conversational sports analytics combining an Agentic SQL Model, a planning harness, and a Feedback Engine.
items.why: Shows a pattern for keeping data agents accurate over time by using runtime execution feedback to guide controlled offline evolution.

items.title: Practice Makes Fluent: Learning to Use Earlier Predictions in Looped Models
items.summary: Researchers propose FLUENT, a method that trains looped models to use earlier intermediate predictions so they exit early and use less computation on tasks.
items.why: Could help teams cut inference compute by letting models learn to stop iterating once early predictions are good enough.

items.title: FlashProve-Next: Verifiable Inference for Production LLM APIs
items.summary: FlashProve-Next proposes zero-knowledge-masked proofs that let clients verify individual responses from closed-weight LLM APIs ran the advertised model and settings.
items.why: Addresses trust in third-party LLM APIs by offering verification of model, precision, and reasoning budget without changing native serving.

items.title: Teaching Students to Stand on Their Own: Distilling Vision Foundation Models for Fine-Grained Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning
items.summary: Researchers study distilling vision foundation models into smaller students for fine-grained few-shot class-incremental learning, noting distilled students struggle with fine-grained recognition.
items.why: Relevant to teams deploying compact vision models that must learn new fine-grained classes from few images.

items.title: ScanAR: Parallel Row-Scan Decoding for Efficient Image Generation in Unified Autoregressive Models
items.summary: ScanAR proposes parallel row-scan decoding to speed up image generation in unified autoregressive multimodal models without changing the tokenizer or prediction head.
items.why: Targets the dominant inference bottleneck of sequential raster-order image token decoding in unified multimodal models.

items.title: Triage Before Fine-Tuning: Feasibility-Gated Selection and Monitored Adaptation of Embodied Foundation Models for a Fixed Physical Platform
items.summary: Researchers examine how to choose and fine-tune embodied foundation models for a fixed physical platform, splitting performance gaps into sensing and latency gaps.
items.why: Gives practitioners a framework for deciding whether benchmark-ranked robot checkpoints will work on their hardware before fine-tuning.

items.title: LSRP*-LA: Scalable and Anytime Multi-Agent Path Finding for Large Agents with Asynchronous Actions
items.summary: Researchers introduce LSRP*-LA, an anytime multi-agent path finding planner that handles large agents with asynchronous actions and scales to many agents.
items.why: Extends practical multi-robot path planning to larger agents and unsynchronized actions common in real warehouse or fleet settings.

items.title: QPAT: A Universal Quantum Machine Learning Framework for Quantum-Assisted Training and Classical Inference
items.summary: Researchers propose QPAT, a quantum machine learning framework that uses quantum-assisted training while keeping classical inference.
items.why: Explores a hybrid path for NISQ hardware, though the text gives limited detail on practical gains.

items.title: KnitNet: Learning to Search at Inference Time for Exact RNA Inverse Design
items.summary: Researchers introduce KnitNet, an inference-time search framework that uses verifier feedback to design RNA sequences that exactly fold into target structures.

items.title: FEAST: Fair and Efficient Adaptive Sampling for Task-Free On-Policy Learning
items.summary: Researchers introduce FEAST, an adaptive sampling method for allocating limited rollout budgets across capabilities in task-free on-policy training of language agents.
items.why: Highlights a feedback loop where under-trained capabilities get fewer rollouts, relevant to teams training self-improving agents.

items.title: When Rerankers Work Together: Better and Faster Reranking without Joint Training
items.summary: Researchers study composing heterogeneous rerankers without joint training and propose lightweight coarse scorers that are both better and faster in multistage RAG pipelines.
items.why: Offers practical guidance for improving retrieval quality and latency in RAG systems without costly retraining.

items.title: Mitigating Overgeneralization in RND via Spectral Target Design
items.summary: Researchers analyze overgeneralization in Random Network Distillation for RL novelty detection and propose a spectral target design to mitigate it.
items.why: Provides a kernel-based explanation and fix for novelty signals collapsing on unfamiliar inputs in RL exploration.

items.title: Random Voronoi Networks
items.summary: Researchers introduce Random Voronoi Networks, structured three-layer MLPs that encode nearest-neighbor geometry via sampled Voronoi comparisons.
items.why: Offers a differentiable alternative to memory-heavy nearest-neighbor methods, though the text gives limited evaluation detail.

items.title: When Are Parallel Subagents Effective for Coding? An Empirical Study on Repository Construction
items.summary: An empirical study compares single coding agents with main agents delegating to parallel subagents on repository-construction tasks, at equal time and equal cost.
items.why: Helps teams decide whether parallel subagent delegation justifies its multiplied run cost for long-horizon coding tasks.

items.title: Correlation-Aware Evidential Fusion for Trusted Multi-View Classification
items.summary: Researchers propose correlation-aware evidential fusion for trusted multi-view classification, accounting for correlated views that repeatedly count the same evidence.

items.title: DiCALM: Converting Autoregressive Convolution-Attention Language Models into Discrete Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Researchers introduce DiCALM, a recipe for converting hybrid convolution-attention LFM2 language models from autoregressive to masked-diffusion text generation.
items.why: It shows a path to reuse existing hybrid AR models for diffusion generation rather than training diffusion models from scratch.

items.title: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures
items.summary: WorldReforge is presented to teach robot world models how manipulation failures like misaligned grasps and slips unfold, after tested models underperformed a static baseline on failure cases.
items.why: Robot world models used for policy evaluation and planning may be unreliable off the success path, which matters for deployment testing.

items.title: Connecting AI Agents to Live Discrete Element Simulations via the Model Context Protocol
items.summary: A Model Context Protocol server lets a general-purpose AI agent operate a discrete element simulation engine while it runs, reading, changing, or stopping the model alongside a human modeler.
items.why: It demonstrates a concrete pattern for connecting agents to live engineering simulation tools through MCP.

items.title: Towards 360$^\circ$ Embodied UAV Tracking Without Turning
items.summary: Researchers introduce 360UAV-ETrack, a simulation benchmark of 2,652 sequences, and 360UAV-TVLA, a panoramic vision-based method for UAV tracking without turning to change heading.
items.why: Full-spherical perception could decouple target tracking from heading control for drones, a benchmark-level result rather than a deployed system.

items.title: InstructTTS-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Objective Instruction-Following TTS
items.summary: InstructTTS-OPD proposes on-policy distillation to jointly optimize instruction following, pronunciation, and naturalness in instruction-following text-to-speech models.
items.why: It addresses the difficulty of balancing multiple objectives under a single scalar reward when post-training TTS models.

items.title: DuoMI: Dual Mutual Information Regularization for Expert Reuse in Looped Transformers
items.summary: DuoMI introduces dual mutual information regularization to encourage expert reuse across rounds in looped mixture-of-experts Transformers.
items.why: Better expert routing across loop iterations could improve parameter efficiency in looped MoE architectures.

items.title: RefMix: Expanding Endpoint Proposals for Diversity-Preserving Reward Fine-Tuning
items.summary: RefMix proposes injecting reference-assisted alternative endpoint candidates into training pools to counter diversity loss in reward fine-tuning of flow-based generative models.
items.why: It targets a feedback loop where reward fine-tuning progressively reduces visual diversity, relevant to training image generators.

items.title: AI Buckingham: Agentic Discovery of Dimensionless Scaling Laws Across Physical Regimes
items.summary: AI Buckingham is an agentic framework pairing an LLM with symbolic and numerical tools to autonomously discover dimensionless scaling laws from problem descriptions and data.

items.title: Embodied-VGGT: Preserving Reliable Local Geometry for Long-Sequence Reconstruction
items.summary: Embodied-VGGT is presented as a method for long-sequence 3D reconstruction that preserves reliable local geometry while correcting accumulated drift during global refinement.
items.why: Drift correction in long-sequence reconstruction matters for robotics and autonomous driving mapping pipelines.

items.title: Fine-Tuning Without Gradients? Closed-Form, LLM-Written Classifiers on a Frozen Encoder
items.summary: Closed-form weight-space programming uses an LLM to write programs that fit closed-form classifier heads on a frozen masked language model, without gradient fine-tuning.
items.why: It suggests a gradient-free alternative to fine-tuning for classification, though the paper's results versus fine-tuning are not stated here.

items.title: Kolpona: An Agentic Framework with Gradient-Free Neuron Programming for RTL Generation
items.summary: Kolpona is an agentic framework that improves open-weight LLMs for RTL Verilog generation via gradient-free neuron programming, keeping edits only when testbench results improve.
items.why: It offers a way to improve hardware-design LLMs without GPU fine-tuning or large verified Verilog corpora.

items.title: MolGPAO: Molecular Generative Pre-trained Autoregressive Octree with Speculative Decoding and Sub-Millisecond Seam Healing for 3D Molecules
items.summary: MolGPAO is a standalone 3D octree autoregressive architecture for molecule generation, adding speculative decoding and seam healing to address geometric and valence issues in prior methods.

items.title: Aegis-VLA: Reliability-Gated Action Refinement via a Trajectory World Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation
items.summary: Aegis-VLA is a world-model-guided vision-language-action framework that generates predictive action corrections for dynamic object manipulation and decides whether to apply them.
items.why: Gating corrections by reliability addresses a practical failure mode for robots manipulating moving objects.

items.title: DosePET: An Open-Source Dataset with 2100 Radiation Dose Maps for PET/CT
items.summary: DosePET is an open-source dataset of 2,100 Monte Carlo-simulated patient-specific absorbed-dose maps from publicly available PET/CT examinations.
items.why: Public dose-map data could enable training AI models for personalized internal dosimetry in nuclear medicine.

items.title: CARROT: Competitive Adaptive Graph Clustering via Semi-Relaxed Optimal Transport
items.summary: CARROT is a deep graph clustering method using semi-relaxed optimal transport to handle unknown cluster counts and highly imbalanced cluster sizes.

items.title: Residual Cross-Model Narrative Convergence under Shared Prompts: Auditing Prompt Controls and Narrative Measurement
items.summary: Researchers analyze 51,240 LLM-generated stories from 10,248 shared prompts, comparing narrative similarity across five models using 213 features.
items.why: It helps teams separate prompt-driven narrative similarity from model-specific writing tendencies when evaluating or auditing generated content.

items.title: Evaluating Ukrainian Grammatical Competence in Language Models: Probability Versus Prompting
items.summary: Researchers released a set of 1,444 Ukrainian minimal pairs and used them to measure grammatical competence across 19 language models.
items.why: Organisations deploying LLMs in Ukrainian-language systems get a released benchmark and protocol for checking whether models produce normative Ukrainian.

items.title: Assessing the Physical Interpretability of AlphaEarth Foundation Embeddings Through Multi-Sensor Satellite Time-Series Benchmarking for Agricultural Mapping
items.summary: Researchers evaluated AlphaEarth Foundation embeddings for agricultural land-use and irrigation-type mapping in Morocco against multi-sensor satellite time-series features.
items.why: It offers evidence on whether pretrained geospatial embeddings can replace costlier time-series feature pipelines for agricultural mapping.

items.title: Incorporating the Knowledge Distillation to Improve the EfficientNet Transfer Learning Capability
items.summary: The paper proposes incorporating knowledge distillation to improve transfer learning capability of EfficientNet models in computer vision.

items.title: Counter-DECEIVR: Counterfactual Explanations for Deepfake Detectors using Detector-Guided Rectified Flow Inversion
items.summary: Researchers introduce Counter-DECEIVR, a method that generates counterfactual explanations for deepfake detectors using detector-guided rectified flow inversion.
items.why: Counterfactual explanations can show analysts which evidence drives a deepfake detector's verdict, helping them decide whether to trust it.

items.title: Post-Training Policy Replication for Strategy-Following Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning across Team Sizes
items.summary: Researchers propose a team-size-independent observation architecture and post-training policy replication for strategy-following multi-agent deep reinforcement learning.
items.why: Reducing retraining costs when team sizes change could make managerially controlled multi-agent RL systems cheaper to scale and transfer.

items.title: Hijacking 3D Generation: Targeted Adversarial Attacks against Image-to-3D Models via Prefix Trajectory Alignment
items.summary: Researchers present a targeted adversarial attack that makes image-to-3D models generate policy-restricted 3D geometry from visually benign inputs, bypassing input inspectors.
items.why: Services relying on input-image inspectors for content policy may be bypassed, exposing generation pipelines to misuse and security risks.

items.title: WorldBridge: Bridging Scattered Views for Coherent 3D World Generation
items.summary: WorldBridge is a framework for generating coherent, controllable 3D worlds from scattered images with little or no visual overlap.

items.title: Whose Side Are You On? A Framework and Benchmark for Assessing LLM Political Stances through Politicians Social Media Posts
items.summary: Researchers propose a framework and WorldPOLL benchmark of 4,600 politicians' X/Twitter posts to assess LLMs' political stances through simulated social media interactions.
items.why: Teams deploying LLMs in political or public-facing contexts can use this framework to measure which stances models consistently express.

items.title: Will AI Replace Juniors? How Task Complexity Reduces Automation Risk
items.summary: A pre-registered survey experiment with managers from 1,435 German firms examines how task complexity affects willingness to replace entry-level labour with AI.
items.why: Leaders planning junior hiring may find that managers view complex, judgement-heavy tasks as less exposed to AI substitution than standardised ones.

items.title: AlignPre: Skill-Aligned Post-Training for Latent-Free Generative Precipitation Nowcasting
items.summary: AlignPre is a pixel-space generative diffusion framework for precipitation nowcasting that aligns post-training with operational forecast skill, without latent compression modules.

items.title: Do Machine Learning Ensembles Beat Published Quotas? Target Parameterization, Censored Baselines, and Conformal Intervals Under Admissions Reform
items.summary: The paper evaluates machine learning and econometric estimators against published Vietnamese university admission quotas using a 2022 to 2026 undergraduate panel.

items.title: SysBio-SR: Benchmarking Symbolic Regression for Trajectory Fidelity and Mechanism Recovery in Systems Biology
items.summary: Researchers introduce SysBio-SR, a benchmark of 198 literature-based biological ODE systems to test whether symbolic regression recovers true reaction mechanisms.
items.why: Shows that accurate trajectory fitting does not guarantee recovery of underlying mechanisms, so evaluation of scientific model-discovery tools needs mechanism-level checks.

items.title: Unstable Action Boundaries in Lethal Drone Agents
items.summary: A study tests whether tool-using LLM drone agents keep stable action boundaries when target descriptors change in a simulated perception-action pipeline over drone imagery.
items.why: Tool-using agents that can trigger high-impact actions may behave unpredictably under small input changes, a safety concern beyond text-only refusal behavior.

items.title: MUSE: Multi-Task Uncertainty-Aware Self-Supervised Encoder for mmWave ISAC
items.summary: MUSE is a multi-task, uncertainty-aware self-supervised encoder for mmWave integrated sensing and communication that aims to support multiple sensing tasks from one model.
items.why: A shared encoder with uncertainty estimates could reduce per-task training and flag unreliable predictions in mmWave sensing systems.

items.title: Out of Sight, Not Out of Clues: Can Video LLMs Guess from Partial Evidence?
items.summary: Researchers argue existing Video LLM benchmarks use a binary answerable-or-unanswerable split, leaving partial visual evidence unmeasured, and propose evaluating responses to partial evidence.
items.why: Engineers deploying video models in surveillance or accessibility need to know whether models answer, guess, or abstain appropriately when evidence is incomplete.

items.title: FoundSurface: Feedforward Ray-Based 3D Scene Surface Reconstruction from Unposed Images
items.summary: FoundSurface is a feedforward pipeline that reconstructs continuous 3D surfaces from unposed images by combining pointmap and ray-based representations.
items.why: It offers a camera-pose-free route to dense 3D surfaces, which could simplify reconstruction pipelines for vision and robotics teams.

items.title: WorldPhy: Benchmarking Fine-Grained Physical Plausibility of World Models in Robotics
items.summary: WorldPhy is a new benchmark for evaluating fine-grained physical plausibility of robotics world models, covering robot motion and object interactions.
items.why: Teams using generated video as world models for robots need finer physics checks than general video-generation benchmarks provide.

items.title: Reproducer Synthesis for AI-Reported Bugs in the Linux Kernel
items.summary: The paper argues that runnable proof-of-concept reproducers should accompany AI-generated bug reports for Linux kernel patches, to help maintainers verify them.
items.why: Maintainers and kernel teams receiving AI review reports could triage faster if each report included a runnable reproducer.

items.title: Lost in the Grid: Where Multimodal LLMs Fail Between Seeing and Planning
items.summary: GridProbe is a diagnostic benchmark that separates visual perception, rule application, and multi-step planning failures in multimodal LLMs on grid games.
items.why: End-to-end success rates hide where spatial planning fails, so this benchmark helps engineers locate the actual weakness in MLLM agents.

items.title: Strategic and Robust Task Allocation for Combat Objectives in Adversarial Multi-Agent Environments
items.summary: Researchers propose a hybrid predict-then-optimize method that uses a masked multi-head model to assign agents to objectives in adversarial team games in real time.
items.why: The approach combines tactical prediction with optimization for multi-agent allocation under uncertainty, relevant to teams building coordinated agent systems.

items.title: Multi-view fnirs identifies neurophysiological subtypes in post-stroke aphasia
items.summary: A study of 79 post-stroke aphasia patients used multi-view fNIRS and unsupervised clustering to identify neurophysiological subtypes.

items.title: Agentic-Level Adversarial Purification: Revisiting Diffusion Purifiers on Native-Resolution Agentic Inputs
items.summary: The paper revisits diffusion purifiers as defenses for vision-language agents on native-resolution inputs, which prior agent defense evaluations did not test.
items.why: Engineers securing vision-language agents against adversarial page perturbations get an evaluation of a plug-in purifier defense they may adopt.

items.title: Hierarchical Semantic Learning for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Missing Modalities
items.summary: Hierarchical Semantic Learning (HSL) is proposed for multimodal sentiment analysis, handling missing modalities by exploiting semantic hierarchy in deep encoders.
items.why: Robust handling of missing sensor or input modalities matters for real-world multimodal systems with unreliable transmission.

items.title: MINE: A Training-Free Defense against Indirect Prompt Injection via Mutual Information and Embedding Variance
items.summary: MINE is a training-free defense against indirect prompt injection in RAG that maximizes relevance via mutual information and embedding variance, and also works as a reranker.
items.why: It offers an attack-agnostic defense that needs no retraining, which is useful for teams running retrieval-augmented systems exposed to injected content.

items.title: Beyond Logits: Coherent Hallucination Mitigation via Attention Contrastive Decoding
items.summary: Attention Contrastive Decoding (ACD) is a training-free plug-in that reduces hallucination in vision-language models by contrasting attention rather than logits.
items.why: It targets hallucination mitigation without degrading generation coherence, a tradeoff that affects deployed LVLM output quality.

items.title: GeoCAM: Self-Supervised Sonar-Optical Representation Learning via Geographic Overlap Supervision
