items.summary: GeoCAM is a geography-guided self-supervised framework that learns representations linking side-scan sonar and underwater optical imagery for benthic habitat understanding.

items.title: The Socratic PAUSE: safeguarding scientific judgement at AI speed
items.summary: The paper argues AI has accelerated scientific discovery far more than justification, and proposes safeguards so researchers evaluate AI-generated evidence before relying on it.
items.why: Research teams adopting generative AI for hypotheses and code need checks that keep confidence tied to evidence.

items.title: Weakly Conditioned Diffusion Model Augmentation for Prostate Segmentation
items.summary: A 2.5D mask-conditioned diffusion model generates synthetic T2-weighted prostate MRI volumes to augment training data for segmentation.
items.why: Synthetic conditioned augmentation can reduce boundary errors and over-segmentation when medical training data is limited and heterogeneous.

items.title: LLM-coupled interpretable tool wear monitoring with multi-evidence reasoning in CNC machining
items.summary: A two-layer framework combines a GRU wear classifier, reporting 98.38% macro F1 on PHM2010, with LLM-generated reports and replacement suggestions for CNC tool wear.
items.why: It shows pairing a classifier with LLM reasoning to produce interpretable maintenance guidance for industrial monitoring systems.

items.title: LatentCP-DPO: Conformal Pessimism for DPO with Finite-Sample Guarantees
items.summary: Researchers introduce LatentCP-DPO, combining conformal prediction with pessimistic preference optimization to reduce DPO overfitting on limited, noisy preference data.
items.why: Offers a finite-sample-guaranteed way to make preference tuning more robust when labeled preference data is scarce or noisy.

items.title: Latent-in-the-Middle: On the Security of Cross-Model Latent Communication in Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: A paper examines the security of cross-model latent communication, where a learned mapper translates one LLM's KV cache for use by another in multi-agent systems.
items.why: Shared internal representations between agents may open security risks that natural-language messaging does not, which matters for multi-agent system design.

items.title: StateWeaver: Multi-Agent Coordination of Story-State Transitions for Long-Horizon Video Generation
items.summary: StateWeaver proposes a multi-agent framework to improve long-video consistency and event-driven state changes in video generation.
items.why: Shows how agentic planning and review loops can address long-horizon consistency limits of current video foundation models.

items.title: WebVibe: Multimodal Interactive Website Generation via Reverse Synthesis and Visual Self-Distillation
items.summary: WebVibe introduces a method for generating interactive multi-page websites from design specs, using reverse synthesis and visual self-distillation.
items.why: Targets known weaknesses in generating stateful, multi-page web apps from multimodal models, relevant to automated front-end tooling.

items.title: RAP: Radial-Angular Random Projection for Hyperbolic Representations
items.summary: RAP proposes a radial-angular random projection method for compressing hyperbolic representations, filling a gap where no analogous primitive to Euclidean random projection existed.
items.why: Provides a dimensionality reduction tool for hyperbolic embeddings used in some Transformers and vision-language models.

items.title: The cost of being seen as AI in group bargaining
items.summary: A study of 2,234 participants in a repeated three-player bargaining game finds players presented as AI received fewer points and were included in fewer final agreements.
items.why: Suggests labeling systems as AI may carry social costs in group decisions, relevant to deploying AI agents in negotiation settings.

items.title: LUDIUS: A Benchmark for Embodied Social Intelligence in Everyday Human-Robot Interactions
items.summary: LUDIUS is a benchmark evaluating vision-language models on embodied social intelligence across 15 skills in everyday human-robot interactions.
items.why: Gives teams a structured way to assess social judgment of VLM-driven robots beyond task success.

items.title: Puzzling-Bench: Evaluating Language Models on 23,777 Human-Written Puzzles with Community-Verified Answers
items.summary: Puzzling-Bench introduces a benchmark of 23,777 community-verified puzzles from Puzzling Stack Exchange, including riddles, ciphers, logic grids, and images.
items.why: Provides a large, human-written reasoning benchmark with verified answers and hints for evaluating language models.

items.title: Inverse Reinforcement Learning with State-Dependent Foresight for Human Decision-Making
items.summary: SC-AIRL is an inverse reinforcement learning method that models bounded, state-dependent human foresight when inferring reward functions from behavior.
items.why: Offers a modeling approach that better fits real human planning horizons, though the text gives little on practical applications.

items.title: ConTra: A Training Framework for Effective Contextual Retrieval via Prefix Generation
items.summary: ConTra is a training framework that improves contextual retrieval by generating text prefixes that keep chunks searchable while preserving document context.
items.why: Addresses a common RAG problem where chunking strips identifying context, relevant to retrieval pipeline design.

items.title: When Skills Fail to Compose: Compatibility and Retention in Language Models
items.summary: A study finds independently learned soft-prompt skills compose poorly in frozen language models, with one-call composition accuracy at most 7.6%.
items.why: Warns that reusable skill libraries built from independently trained soft prompts may not compose reliably without explicit intermediate outputs.

items.title: SemProxy: Semantic 3D Proxies for Controllable Agentic 3D Modeling
items.summary: SemProxy proposes labeled 3D bounding boxes as an intermediate representation letting users specify object parts and spatial intent for coding agents generating 3D models.
items.why: Offers a more precise control interface for agentic 3D modeling than text prompts and reference images alone.

items.title: CHASE: Curiosity-Guided Skill Acquisition for Embodied Task Execution
items.summary: CHASE is a curiosity-guided framework that lets robots formulate hypotheses, seek evidence, and acquire missing skills during task execution.
items.why: Describes an approach for robots to handle incomplete skills in partially observed environments, though practical details are limited in the text.

items.title: Calibration of Neuromusculoskeletal Models Using Differentiable Physics: Recommendations for Improving Model Accuracy
items.summary: A paper offers recommendations for improving the accuracy of neuromusculoskeletal model calibration using differentiable physics.

items.title: One Representation to Rule Them All -- Open-Vocabulary Change Detection from Text or Visual Examples
items.summary: OVTSID3 is a training-free framework that unifies region grouping, concept identification, and temporal comparison for open-vocabulary change detection from text or visual examples.
items.why: Removes the need for several separate intermediate models in change detection, simplifying detection pipelines.

items.title: Most of the Way There: Turning a Strong Video Prior into an Action-Conditioned World Model
items.summary: Researchers describe turning a strong video generation prior into an action-conditioned world model that simulates how the world responds to specific robot actions.
items.why: It offers a path to scalable robot policy evaluation and improvement without costly real-world rollouts, though the excerpt gives limited detail on results.

items.title: ProxyGenBench: Benchmarking Proxy-Guided Video Generation
items.summary: Researchers introduce ProxyGenBench, a benchmark for video generation guided by structural proxies such as animated 3D blockouts.
items.why: It gives teams a standard way to test whether generators preserve layout and motion intent while fixing proxy artifacts and binding text, image, and audio conditions.

items.title: Noise threshold for learning with quantum memory
items.summary: A paper shows that for Pauli memory noise, quantum memory's learning advantage depends on a sum of squared eigenvalues, with a noise threshold for exponential gains.
items.why: It clarifies noise limits for quantum learning hardware, though its direct relevance to most engineering teams is limited.

items.title: Angular Interpolation in Sparse-View Low-Dose CT Reconstruction: Placement Effects and Data-Consistency Step-Size Scaling
items.summary: A study on sparse-view low-dose CT reconstruction examines how angular interpolation placement and data-consistency step sizes affect dual-domain network performance.
items.why: It offers practical guidance for preprocessing choices in medical imaging reconstruction pipelines, based on synthetic parallel-beam data.

items.title: Long-Horizon Planning with Latent World Models via Graph Anchors
items.summary: Researchers propose graph anchors to improve long-horizon planning with latent world models, addressing failures of latent distance as a planning metric.
items.why: It identifies specific failure modes of latent-distance planners in robotics, which matter for teams building model-based manipulation systems.

items.title: PURA: Video Token Pruning via Unified Spatiotemporal Redundancy Assessment
items.summary: PURA is a training-free method that prunes video tokens by jointly assessing spatial and temporal redundancy in video large language models.
items.why: Reducing long visual token sequences without retraining can lower inference costs for video LLM deployments.

items.title: EPPC-CARE: Staged Hierarchical Annotation of Communication Behaviors in Secure Patient-Provider Messages
items.summary: EPPC-CARE is an automated framework for annotating communication behaviors in secure patient-provider portal messages, evaluated on 867 messages.
items.why: It shows how automated annotation can reduce manual labor in analyzing clinical messaging, relevant to health-tech builders.

items.title: HAS: Hierarchical Adaptive Frame Sampling for Video Understanding
items.summary: HAS is a hierarchical adaptive frame sampling method that helps multimodal LLMs choose video frames for queries needing either holistic or fine-grained understanding.
items.why: Better frame selection can improve video understanding accuracy within fixed context-length limits.

items.title: Recalling the Past to Answer the Present: Context-Aware Multi-Evidence Reasoning for Streaming Video Question Answering
items.summary: StreamRecall is a benchmark testing vision-language models on answering context-dependent questions over temporally scattered evidence in streaming video.
items.why: It exposes limits of current offline-evaluated video QA models in real-time streaming scenarios that product teams may target.

items.title: An Information-Theoretic Analysis of Information Hiding in Semantic Communication
items.summary: The paper develops an information-theoretic framework for information hiding within semantic communication, extending classical hiding models to a semantic layer.
items.why: The text gives little on practical implications; it is primarily theoretical work on semantic communication security.

items.title: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
items.summary: Sage-Med-Preview, a 35B-parameter medical multimodal model, is introduced alongside findings that scaling mainly improves text rather than visual capabilities.
items.why: The finding that medical MLLMs trail general models on visual tasks and scaling doesn't fix this is useful for healthcare AI planning.

items.title: Tune for Retention, Not Just Gain: SFT Forgets Far Less than You Think
items.summary: The paper argues that supervised fine-tuning forgets far less than assumed when hyperparameters such as lower learning rates are chosen for retention.
items.why: Teams fine-tuning LLMs can reduce catastrophic forgetting through hyperparameter choices rather than switching to on-policy methods.

items.title: VisualMontage: Manipulating the Beliefs of Vision-Language Agents with Authentic Image Sequences
items.summary: VisualMontage introduces a benchmark of 544 target cases showing how coordinated posts with authentic images and faithful captions can steer vision-language agents toward attacker-chosen claims.
items.why: It highlights a manipulation risk for VLM agents that interpret social media, relevant to anyone deploying agents on untrusted content.

items.title: From Models to Services: Systematizing Security Assurance for Model-as-a-Service
items.summary: A paper systematizes security research for Model-as-a-Service, decomposing it into five layers and trust boundaries and evaluating 50 defenses across 120 studies.
items.why: It offers a structured threat model for teams securing cloud-hosted LLM services and choosing defenses.

items.title: DecisionReplay: A Corpus and Offline Simulator for Ensembling Decision Models
items.summary: DecisionReplay releases a corpus of probability vectors from 17 commercial decision models across 35 benchmarks, with cost and latency data, for offline simulation.
items.why: Engineers can simulate ensembles, routers, and cascades offline without new model calls, cutting evaluation cost.

items.title: LatentRL-QAS: Transfer via Latent Reinforcement Learning for Quantum Architecture Search
items.summary: Researchers introduced LatentRL-QAS, a latent-space framework that lets reinforcement learning agents for quantum architecture search transfer learning across different qubit counts.
items.why: Transfer across qubit counts could cut the cost of automated quantum circuit design, though the impact is limited to quantum computing research.

items.title: Carrying Feature Ablations Across Sparse Autoencoder Seeds
items.summary: Researchers study how to carry feature ablations from one sparse autoencoder trained with a given random seed to another, since SAEs with different seeds learn different features.
items.why: Feature matching across SAE seeds affects whether interpretability edits to vision encoders transfer reliably, which matters for model editing workflows.

items.title: Motion Beyond Pixels: Learning Future Visual Representations for Object-Centric Dynamics
items.summary: Researchers present MotionRep, a world model that jointly predicts future DINO visual representations and 3D object flow for object-centric dynamics in embodied settings.
items.why: Predicting semantic and geometric features rather than raw RGB may help robots plan motion, though the text gives little on practical deployment.

items.title: Do We Still Need Reinforcement Learning When We Can Read the World Model?
items.summary: The paper explores having LLM-based coding agents write control policies directly by reasoning over readable world models and environment source code, bypassing conventional reinforcement learning.
items.why: If coding agents can derive policies from readable world models, teams could reduce interaction data needs, but the text gives limited evidence of performance.

items.title: Multi-Party Authorization of Maintenance Prescriptions on a Permissioned Blockchain
items.summary: Researchers propose requiring permissioned-blockchain endorsers to verify succinct proofs of model calculations before approving maintenance prescriptions, tested on a four-organization Hyperledger Fabric setup.
items.why: Verifiable proofs could let multi-party industrial workflows confirm that recommendations actually came from the agreed model and decision rule.

items.title: DemoFoundry: Toward Scalable Photorealistic Robot Data with Coding Agents and Generative Rendering
items.summary: DemoFoundry couples coding agents with generative rendering to automatically synthesize photorealistic, physically grounded robot demonstrations with aligned action labels.
items.why: Automated generation of realistic robot training data could reduce the cost of scaling robot learning beyond human demonstrations.

items.title: RoboEvo$^2$: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution
items.summary: RoboEvo² proposes a framework where robot reasoning agents and vision-language-action policies co-evolve recursively, so robots improve skills through interaction and practice.
items.why: Co-evolving reasoning agents and control policies could reduce reliance on human demonstrations for robots in unfamiliar settings.

items.title: Find the Clue, Not the Scene: Rethinking Reasoning for Entity Recognition in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Analysis of thinking vision-language models finds that entity recognition is the main bottleneck in knowledge-based visual question answering, accounting for 76.3% of errors.
items.why: Recognition, not reasoning, drives most errors, suggesting teams should focus on visual grounding when building VLM-based QA systems.

items.title: Evacuation Traffic Prediction for Dynamic Transportation Networks over Multiple Hurricanes: A Generalized Graph Learning Approach
items.summary: Researchers propose a generalized graph learning approach to predict evacuation traffic on highways across multiple hurricanes using detector-based transportation network data.
items.why: The text gives limited detail on results, so its relevance for engineers is unclear beyond transportation forecasting use cases.

items.title: Maco-RL: Scaling Agent Capabilities with Mixed-Task Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Maco-RL proposes a method to scale mixed-task reinforcement learning, training a unified agent policy across domains with quota-based scheduling and continual domain expansion.
items.why: Training one policy across multiple task domains without separate specialists or distillation could simplify agent training pipelines.

items.title: When the Proxy Is Wrong: Mismatch-Corrected Bandits for Adaptive Data Sampling
items.summary: Researchers model the mismatch between small proxy models and larger target models as a multi-fidelity bandit for adaptive training data selection.
items.why: Correcting for proxy-target ranking mismatch could improve data selection efficiency when small models guide training of larger ones.

items.title: How Well Do Vision-Language Scene Graphs Serve as Memory for Embodied Question Answering?
items.summary: A study defines answerability for vision-language scene graphs used as memory in embodied question answering, showing targeted repairs raise answerability from 27.2% to 37.4%.
items.why: Better object recall does not always improve answerability, so teams building graph-based memory should measure answer utility directly.

items.title: Collect for Coverage, Replay with Evidence: Adaptive and Efficient On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary: Researchers propose an adaptive method for on-policy distillation in long-horizon agents that reuses stored prefix histories to reduce costly fresh environment rollouts.
items.why: Reducing rollout costs for long-horizon agent training could make distillation practical for teams with limited environment compute.

items.title: Reading Fine-Tuning Diffs Through Lenses: Model Diffing for Backdoor Detection
items.summary: Researchers introduce a scoring system based on token readouts to compare weight, activation, and output-based model diffing methods for detecting backdoors in fine-tuned models.
items.why: Standardized comparison of diffing methods gives security teams a clearer basis for checking whether fine-tuning introduced a backdoor.

items.title: One Model, Many Modes: Evolving System Prompt Ensembles for Creative Generation
items.summary: Researchers formalize creative generation as a multi-objective optimization and propose evolving system prompt ensembles to produce responses that are both high-quality and novel.
items.why: Ensembles of system prompts could help teams counter mode collapse in aligned LLMs when they need diverse, original outputs.

items.title: InterConRank: Joint Node Centrality in Interconnected Heterogeneous Networks
items.summary: Researchers introduce InterConRank, a centrality algorithm that ranks nodes separately in each layer of interconnected heterogeneous networks, letting cross-layer neighbors shift scores.
items.why: Offers a way to rank node importance in multi-layer graphs where same-layer connections alone miss cross-layer influence.

items.title: Make the Adversary Spend More: Stateful Deception as a Cost-Exchange Primitive for AI-Era Cyber Defense
items.summary: Researchers propose stateful cyber deception that keeps each recognized adversary in a persistent, coherent fake environment to raise attackers' costs.
items.why: Suggests defenders can judge deception by cost imposed on LLM-enabled attackers rather than realism or detection rates.

items.title: When Every Rollout Fails: Splicing Learner-Conditioned Options into Long-Horizon Agent RL
items.summary: SPLICE constructs local training targets from failed policy trajectories online, helping group-based RL on long-horizon agent tasks where every rollout fails.
items.why: Addresses zero-gradient failure in RL for long-horizon agents without relying on expensive full expert trajectories.

items.title: PersonaFactory: Stylistic User Prompt Augmentation with Synthetic Persona Bank
items.summary: PersonaFactory is a pipeline that generates synthetic user personas to augment prompts, producing a bank of over 740,000 stylistically varied user prompts.
items.why: Could improve synthetic training and evaluation data that currently sounds monolingual and stylistically flat.

items.title: HOG-WAM: Improving Visual Robustness through Future Gradient Prediction
items.summary: HOG-WAM adds future Histograms of Oriented Gradients as training-only supervision to world-action models to improve policy robustness against visual corruption.
items.why: Offers a training-time fix for robot policies failing under visual corruption, with no added inference cost.

items.title: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models
items.summary: A study compares coding agents against video generation models on visual reasoning tasks under matched conditions, finding code-based solving stronger.
items.why: Suggests symbolic code execution may be more reliable than video generation for visual reasoning tasks.

items.title: Transferring Architecture as an Optimization Prior
items.summary: The paper investigates whether a network can change its optimization prior by referencing a different architecture during initialization.
items.why: Explores how initialization geometry shapes training, a question relevant to model design and training efficiency.

items.title: Not all world models can doubt: how training objective and architecture shape epistemic uncertainty in JEPA and RSSM world models
items.summary: An empirical study examines how training objectives and architectures shape epistemic uncertainty in JEPA and RSSM world models.
items.why: Helps teams choose world model architectures and objectives based on how reliably they signal unfamiliar situations.

items.title: Probing Visual Idiosyncrasies in Text-to-Image Models
items.summary: Researchers show a standard ResNet-50 can identify which frontier text-to-image model produced an image, indicating models retain distinct visual signatures.
items.why: Relevant to attribution and to evaluations that assume anonymity of model outputs.

items.title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents
items.summary: DRBench Pro is a benchmark that evaluates deep research agents primarily on structured knowledge coverage, built from Wikipedia-derived knowledge trees.
items.why: Gives teams a knowledge-coverage metric for evaluating research agents beyond overall report quality.

items.title: From Prediction to Decision: Decision-Focused Fine-Tuning of Autoregressive Tabular Transformers for Cost-Sensitive Financial Events
items.summary: The paper fine-tunes autoregressive tabular transformers on the decision objective with asymmetric costs for financial event prediction such as fraud.
items.why: Suggests fine-tuning for cost-sensitive decisions may beat post-hoc thresholding of calibrated probabilities in fraud systems.

items.title: BOP-Refer: Benchmark for Monocular 3D and 2D Object Grounding
items.summary: BOP-Refer introduces a benchmark for monocular 3D and 2D grounding of objects, evaluating 17 frontier VLMs with the best model named Gemini 4 Car...
items.why: Shows current VLMs' limits on 3D object grounding from single images, relevant to robotics and industrial vision.

items.title: RePace: Reasoning about Demonstration Speedup for Faster Vision-Language-Action Policies
items.summary: RePace reasons about demonstration speedup, assigning varying speed factors within segments to accelerate vision-language-action policy training data.
items.why: Offers a way to speed up VLA policies without adding a speed-selection module at deployment.

items.title: A Survey of Security, Privacy, and Ethics of Large Language Models in Telecom
items.summary: A survey reviews security, privacy, and ethical risks of LLMs in telecom, introducing a telecom-specific taxonomy linking risks to use cases.
items.why: Useful checklist for telecom teams deploying LLMs on sensitive longitudinal customer and network data.

items.title: Shape-Aware Three-Way Merge for RDF Knowledge Graphs: The schema defines the conflict: an implementation and evaluation
items.summary: The paper presents a shape-aware three-way merge for RDF knowledge graphs that uses SHACL shapes to define conflicts, implemented in a production multi-agent system.
items.why: Provides a schema-driven approach to resolving merge conflicts in knowledge graphs maintained by multiple agents or editors.

items.title: How Much Do Coding Agents Over-Edit, and Why? An Empirical Study of Unneeded Edits in Repository-Level Agent Patches
items.summary: Researchers introduce Delta Residue Attribution to test whether extra edits in agent patches are needed, applying it to 7,660 resolved GitHub Copilot CLI trajectories across 18 models.
items.why: It separates necessary from unneeded agent edits, offering a way to judge whether coding agents' larger patches are actually wasteful.

items.title: Interpretable and Accurate Hybrid Decision Trees with Selective Case-Based Splits
items.summary: Researchers present two hybrid decision tree methods that selectively combine different split strategies, including case-based splits, to improve interpretability and accuracy.

items.title: Enhancing Maritime Domain Awareness using Latent Space Representations
items.summary: Researchers apply compressed Earth Observation embeddings from the TerraMind geospatial model to Maritime Domain Awareness, probing latent representations instead of raw Sentinel-1 imagery.
items.why: Working on compressed latent embeddings rather than raw imagery addresses data volume bottlenecks in operational Earth observation pipelines.

items.title: $\mu$-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents
items.summary: Researchers introduce μ-Bench, a benchmark for voice agents completing joint tasks with multiple users in full-duplex, closed-loop interaction across 20 domains and 100 scenarios.
items.why: It targets multi-user voice agent evaluation, where per-user permissions and privacy constraints make single-user benchmarks insufficient.

items.title: Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces for Hard Math Problems
items.summary: Researchers propose DART, a method that mines diverse alternative reasoning traces from rejected solutions to build training data for hard math problems.
items.why: It offers a way to generate more training signal for math reasoning when verified correct traces are rare.

items.title: Attack Policy Selection can Mislead Monitor Evaluators
items.summary: A study finds that the choice of attack policy strongly affects measured false negative rates when evaluating an ex-production OpenAI AI monitor, ranging from 0.5% to 20.8%.
items.why: Monitor evaluation results depend heavily on how attack transcripts are generated, so safety metrics may be misleading.

items.title: Spectrum Adaptation of AI-Native Autoencoder Communications with Transfer Learning
items.summary: Researchers study autoencoder-based physical-layer communications, showing models trained on AWGN degrade on Rayleigh fading and proposing transfer learning to adapt spectrum conditions.

items.title: MathConstruct: Challenging LLM Reasoning with Constructive Proofs
items.summary: MathConstruct is a benchmark of 121 competition math problems targeting constructive proofs, aimed at reducing saturation and guessing in existing LLM math evaluations.
items.why: Existing math benchmarks are saturated, so constructive-proof benchmarks give teams a harder test of model reasoning.

items.title: MathArena: Evaluating LLMs on Uncontaminated Math Competitions
items.summary: MathArena is a benchmark that evaluates LLMs on recent, uncontaminated math competitions and includes proof-writing tasks.
items.why: Freshly sourced competition problems reduce memorization concerns when comparing models' mathematical reasoning.

items.title: K12Vista: Exploring the Boundaries of MLLMs in K-12 Education
items.summary: K12Vista is a multimodal benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on Chinese K-12 educational content, covering more subjects and question types than prior work.

items.title: Beyond Moral Performance: Empirical Assessment of LLMs' Moral Competence Through Judgment Stability
items.summary: Researchers test 16 LLM configurations for moral competence by measuring stability of framework preferences when morally irrelevant features of dilemmas are varied.

items.title: ReviewSense: Cluster-Guided Evidence Selection for Actionable Review-to-Advice Generation
items.summary: ReviewSense is a workflow that clusters customer reviews with embeddings and LLMs to generate actionable advice, evaluated on dental and healthcare service reviews.

items.title: Semantic Gravity Wells: Why Negative Constraints Backfire
items.summary: A mechanistic study of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct examines why negative constraints such as 'do not use word X' fail, introducing a measure called semantic pressure.
items.why: Explains a common instruction-following failure mode, useful for teams relying on negative prompt constraints.

items.title: HLA: Hadamard Linear Attention
items.summary: Researchers propose Hadamard Linear Attention, a linear attention variant that aims to approximate softmax attention more closely than standard low-degree kernel methods.

items.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Cognitive Complexity in LLMs via Linear Probing using Bloom's Taxonomy
items.summary: A study probes LLM residual streams with linear classifiers to test whether Bloom's Taxonomy cognitive levels, from recall to synthesis, are linearly separable.

items.title: VibeServe: Can AI Agents Build Bespoke LLM Serving Systems?
items.summary: VibeServe, an agentic loop, lets coding agents generate complete bespoke LLM serving stacks end-to-end, planning design search and checking correctness and performance.
items.why: Suggests agents may automate building workload-specific inference infrastructure that today relies on hand-tuned general-purpose serving stacks.

items.title: Search-E1: Self-Distillation Drives Self-Evolution in Search-Augmented Reasoning
items.summary: Search-E1 is a self-evolution framework that alternates GRPO reinforcement learning with on-policy self-distillation to train search-augmented reasoning agents.
items.why: Offers a training recipe for search agents that learns from their own successful trajectories rather than relying on stronger external teachers.

items.title: Personalize-then-Store: Benchmarking and Learning Personalized Memory for Long-horizon Agents
items.summary: Researchers introduce PerMemBench, a benchmark for learning personalized memory policies so LLM agents store user-specific context instead of applying universal static rules.
items.why: Highlights that static memory policies waste budget on transient interactions, a design concern for long-running agent memory.

items.title: Towards Faithful Agentic XAI: A Verification Method and an Open-World Benchmark for Better Model Faithfulness
items.summary: The paper proposes FAX, a verification method that decomposes draft explanations to improve faithfulness of agentic explainable AI, plus an open-world benchmark.
items.why: Shows LLM-based explanation layers can amplify unfaithful outputs, so teams need verification before trusting agent-generated model explanations.

items.title: Benchmark Everything Everywhere All at Once
items.summary: BenchHarness is introduced to automate benchmark construction for LLMs and multimodal LLMs by reusing annotated datasets with agent-based tooling.
items.why: Could reduce the cost of building fresh evaluations as existing benchmarks approach saturation.

items.title: A History-Aware Visually Grounded Critic for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: HiViG is a history-aware, visually grounded critic that evaluates actions before execution for Computer Use Agents, aiming to catch wrong clicks and forgotten earlier steps.
items.why: Pre-execution critics may reduce costly mistakes for GUI agents, though the abstract gives no quantitative results here.

items.title: Are You Still the Agent I Authorized? Earned Authority under a Fixed Ceiling for Evolving Agents
items.summary: The paper examines authorization for long-lived agents that evolve after deployment, arguing that changes can make a previously approved grant no longer match the agent acting under it.
items.why: Raises a concrete governance problem for enterprises granting tool-using agents ongoing authority as they change.

items.title: Fisher-R1: Training LLM Agents for Reliable Hypothesis Testing
items.summary: Fisher-R1 trains LLM agents for statistically valid hypothesis testing, after showing agents often make subtle inferential errors despite correctly executed analyses.
items.why: Shows agents can produce wrong conclusions even with correct code, so p-value validity needs checking beyond execution success.

items.title: iBrain: A Unified Foundation Model Reading the Brain from Surface to Spikes
items.summary: iBrain is a unified foundation model that jointly pretrains on intracranial EEG and intracortical spiking activity from heterogeneous invasive neural recordings.
items.why: Limited relevance to typical engineering work; mainly of interest to neurotech and biomedical ML teams.

items.title: SpecRead: A Benchmark for Measuring Whether Language Models Understand Hardware Specifications
items.summary: SpecRead is a 383-question benchmark testing whether LLMs understand hardware specifications, separately from their ability to generate RTL code.
items.why: Isolates spec comprehension from code generation, helping teams diagnose whether hardware design failures stem from misreading specs.

items.title: Agent Calibration under Deployment Change: Acceptance Contracts, Trajectory Repair, and Adaptation Costs
items.summary: The paper defines agent calibration as qualifying an agent against a versioned deployment contract after a model, tool, or user-context change.
items.why: Gives teams a framework for checking whether agents keep required capabilities when models or tools are swapped.

items.title: FinAutoRubric: Expert-Guided Automatic Rubric Generation for Evaluating Financial Research Agents
items.summary: FinAutoRubric generates evaluation rubrics for financial research agents, with experts specifying reusable guidance that agents and code apply per query.
items.why: Offers a way to evaluate domain agents against institution-specific standards without costly fixed per-item rubrics.

items.title: ACTR: Aligning Thoughts and Responses for Multilingual Safety in Reasoning LLMs
items.summary: ACTR proposes aligning reasoning traces and final responses to improve multilingual safety in reasoning LLMs facing jailbreaks in non-high-resource languages.
items.why: Shows safety of reasoning models can differ across languages even when traces identify risks, relevant for global deployments.

items.title: CompMat-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Computational Materials Science
items.summary: CompMat-Bench is a 94-task benchmark for AI agents in computational materials science, derived from published studies with pre-reproduced research steps.
items.why: Provides a reusable, cheaper way to evaluate scientific agents without rerunning expensive simulations each trial.

items.title: FluidPD: In-Place Elasticity for SLO-Aware Prefill-Decode Disaggregated LLM Serving
items.summary: FluidPD is a prefill-decode disaggregated LLM serving system that adds SLO-aware in-place elasticity to shift capacity between prefill and decode workers during workload shifts.
items.why: Addresses latency SLO violations from fixed prefill/decode ratios without waiting for slow autoscaling or spare GPUs.

items.title: SearchWorld: Spatial Value-Grounded Imagination for UAV Object Search via World Models
items.summary: Researchers propose SearchWorld, a world-model approach for UAV object search in urban areas under partial observability, using spatial value-grounded imagination.
items.why: Offers a planning approach for embodied drone search in cluttered 3D environments, relevant to teams building autonomous aerial systems.

items.title: Where Can a Decision Model Diagnose HVAC Faults? Reasoning Demand, Physical Representation, and Robustness Under Shift
items.summary: A study evaluates whether pretrained decision models, which output probabilities over allowed answers, can diagnose HVAC faults without task-specific training.
items.why: Suggests one pretrained model might serve multiple building-operations decisions without labeled data, though the abstract's findings are cut off.

items.title: RAN-JEPA: An Action-Conditioned World Model for Energy-efficient Mobile Network Control
items.summary: RAN-JEPA is an action-conditioned world model for mobile network control that learns representations from passive telemetry before learning interventions.
items.why: Addresses scarce controlled action data in telecom networks by pretraining on abundant passive telemetry, a useful pattern for energy-efficient network control.

items.title: OwlSight: A Panoramic Monitor for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
items.summary: OwlSight introduces Factor, a Chain-of-Thought monitoring strategy that lets a single monitor cover multiple tasks by customizing monitoring factors in the prompt.
items.why: Offers a way for teams to oversee reasoning models across varied tasks with one monitor rather than task-specific tooling.

items.title: Kairos: Fast and Reliable Symbolic Task Planning for Autonomous Robots
items.summary: Kairos is a single symbolic task planner for robots that handles PDDL features including durative actions, numeric resources, time windows, and continuous change.
items.why: A unified planner for expressive PDDL fragments could simplify robotics stacks that currently need multiple planners with differing failure semantics.

items.title: Researcher-in-the-Loop Evolutionary Discovery of Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Code Families
items.summary: Researchers present a researcher-in-the-loop pipeline combining LLM-guided program evolution with exact evaluation and verification to discover entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting code families.
items.why: Shows a pattern for pairing LLM-driven program search with rigorous verification, though the item is mainly of interest to quantum coding researchers.

items.title: AceAction-5M: Hierarchical Goals for Generalist Action Learning Across 3D Game Worlds
items.summary: AceAction-5M is a dataset of human gameplay across multiple 3D games, organized around hierarchical goals for vision-language-action learning.
items.why: Provides a game-derived VLA dataset with subgoal structure, a lower-cost data source for training generalist action models.

items.title: ConceptARC at Scale: Studying Conceptual Understanding in Reasoning Models
items.summary: A study examines whether large reasoning models form generalizable abstractions across conceptually related ARC tasks, scaling up the ConceptARC benchmark.
items.why: Clarifies how far reasoning models generalize abstract concepts beyond individual tasks, informing expectations for model reasoning reliability.

items.title: Measuring Generative AI Content in Political Campaigns: Evidence of Rising Adoption and Non-Disclosure
items.summary: A study measures how political campaigns produce and circulate AI-generated content during an election cycle, finding rising adoption and non-disclosure.
items.why: Highlights gaps between AI content use and disclosure rules, relevant to teams building provenance or disclosure compliance tooling.

items.title: The WoW: A Large-Scale World Knowledge Corpus for Full-Lifecycle LLM Training
items.summary: WoW is a large-scale Chinese educational world-knowledge corpus built on an Educational Knowledge Graph for full-lifecycle foundation model training.
items.why: A structured, curated Chinese education dataset could be useful for training or evaluating domain-specific models, though the abstract gives limited detail.

items.title: RSI-PDEbench: A Benchmark for Self-Improving Agents in PDE Solving
items.summary: RSI-PDEbench is a benchmark of 1,001 cases across 42 PDE templates for testing whether LLM agents can automate PDE identification and solving.
items.why: Provides a concrete benchmark for evaluating agent automation of scientific computing workflows under noise and distribution shift.

items.title: $\varepsilon$-WM: Error-Driven Dynamics Adaptation across Fast--Slow Timescales for World Modeling
items.summary: ε-WM is a world model that adapts to sudden, persistent robot dynamics changes across fast and slow timescales using error-driven updates.
items.why: Targets a practical failure mode where world-model prediction errors accumulate in rollouts and degrade robot control.

items.title: AutoE2E: Don't speak - Language free end-to-end autonomy for L2++ ADAS and L4 Robotaxis
items.summary: AutoE2E is an open-source end-to-end driving model from the Autoware Foundation Robotaxi Working Group using temporal BEV architecture with about 79.9M parameters.
items.why: An open-source end-to-end autonomy reference for ADAS and robotaxi work gives engineers a concrete architecture to study and build on.

items.title: Auditable Clinical Support with Decision Agents
items.summary: Decision2Care is a decision agent that outputs probabilities for each option and diagnosed 546 emergency admissions across 12 diseases with 86.5% accuracy.
items.why: Shows probability-outputting agents can be faster and more auditable than language-model agents in a high-stakes clinical setting, though it remains a research result.

items.title: KnowMe Paper Radar: Lightweight Discovery of Promising Papers in the Age of Autoresearch
items.summary: KnowMe Paper Radar proposes a lightweight method for discovering promising preprints by using author and institution track records amid rising autoresearch output.
items.why: Addresses discovery problems as LLM-assisted papers multiply, though the abstract provides little on results or tools.

items.title: Can Vision-Language Models Synthesize Executable Game-Playing Programs?
items.summary: A revised arXiv paper asks whether vision-language models can synthesize executable programs that play games, rather than choosing actions step by step.
items.why: It suggests agents might write game-playing code from visual input instead of querying the model before every action, which could cut inference costs in deployment.

items.title: Neur2BiLO: Neural Bilevel Optimization
items.summary: A revised arXiv paper introduces Neur2BiLO, a neural approach to constrained bilevel optimization with integer variables, which is hard for existing exact solvers.
items.why: Exact solvers scale poorly and generalize badly to nonlinear cases, so a learned method could help teams solve hard leader-follower decision problems.

items.title: Polyrating: A Cost-Effective and Bias-Aware Rating System for LLM Evaluation
items.summary: A revised arXiv paper proposes Polyrating, a rating system for LLM human evaluation that accounts for bias, needs less preference data, and compares ratings across tasks.
items.why: Teams running LLM evaluations could get more reliable model rankings from fewer expensive human judgments while controlling for evaluator bias.

items.title: Swarms, Flocks, Gangs: How to build, train, and evaluate multi-agent systems
items.summary: A Hugging Face guide on how to build, train, and evaluate multi-agent systems.
items.why: Offers a practical starting point for engineers designing multi-agent architectures, though the description gives no specifics on methods.

items.title: S&P considers Nvidia credit downgrade over governance and ‘key man’ risks
items.summary: S&P is considering lowering Nvidia's credit rating to AA-, the fourth-highest rating, citing governance and 'key man' risks.
items.why: Credit rating pressure on a major AI chip supplier could affect its borrowing costs and signal investor concern about leadership dependence.

items.title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
items.summary: Google filed a patent for 'My Channel,' a system for personalized, AI-generated video feeds and ads; the patent was rejected, though Google may appeal or resubmit.

items.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
items.summary: The New York Times reportedly warned photographers not to update Photoshop because of its AI features.
items.why: Highlights enterprise and professional users weighing the risks of software updates that add AI features.

items.title: OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work
items.summary: OpenAI is merging its ChatGPT Chat and Work experiences and introducing a single usage meter, so heavy users may hit limits sooner.
items.why: Unified usage metering across merged products affects how teams budget and plan access to ChatGPT.

items.title: Jensen Huang broke Nvidia’s code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it
items.summary: Reporting says Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang broke the company's code of conduct, and that employees may not forget it.
items.why: Leadership conduct lapses at a dominant AI vendor may shape internal culture and talent retention across the industry.

items.title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI ‘absurd’
items.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called rivals' accusations that he favors surrendering human agency to AI 'absurd.'

items.title: Where scientists draw the line on AI agents
items.summary: Hugging Face published an article on where scientists draw the line on AI agents.

items.title: Backblaze explains why it's sharing customer information with advertisers
items.summary: Backblaze told Ars Technica it is sharing customer information with advertisers but says it will not share users' backup or storage files.
items.why: Engineers storing data with cloud providers should understand what customer information is shared and what stays protected.

items.title: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York
items.summary: New York has banned AI chatbot toys for five years, citing Common Sense Media research that found safety failures including exposure to inappropriate content.

items.title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
items.summary: The FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites under its 'Starmind' initiative, the agency's first approval of orbital AI data centers.
items.why: Orbital AI data center approvals signal a new infrastructure direction, though the plan's technical and commercial feasibility remains untested.

items.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
items.summary: State attorneys general challenged Character.AI's proposed bankruptcy sale of users' private chats, which includes data from over 21 million U.S. accounts, 2.1 million tied to minors.
items.why: Sale of sensitive chat data highlights privacy and data-handling risks engineers must address when building consumer AI products.

items.title: New York bans AI toys, including those using internet to talk to children
items.summary: New York has banned AI toys, including those that use the internet to talk with children.
items.why: Signals state-level regulation of consumer AI products aimed at children, which product teams building conversational AI should track.

items.title: Nothing offers a full look at its AI earbuds and charging case
items.summary: Nothing previewed its upcoming Ear Note AI earbuds, which can record calls and whose charging case can record, transcribe, and summarize conversations, ahead of a December 8 release.

items.title: AI data centers are becoming harder to build, and neoclouds are feeling it
items.summary: Neocloud providers report construction delays and costlier debt as Nvidia says it won't backstop AI data centers until they are nearly ready to run.
items.why: Delays and financing hurdles for AI data centers affect capacity planning, with land, power, and finished buildings now key to securing support.

items.title: Amazon is reportedly in talks to end Muse AI shopping block
items.summary: Amazon reportedly held talks about letting Meta's Muse AI agent shop on its marketplace, which could end Amazon's block on Muse.
items.why: Shows how retailers may restrict or admit AI shopping agents, with ad revenue and product recommendations at stake.

items.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift blockade on AI agent Muse
items.summary: Amazon and Meta are reportedly discussing a deal that would lift a two-month blockade on Meta's AI agent Muse.
items.why: Signals that access to major marketplaces for third-party AI shopping agents remains negotiated rather than settled.
